chunks.name: Samar Island
chunks.text: Samar is the third largest island in the Philippines, after Mindanao and Luzon islands. It is located next to Leyte Island and the two are joined by a bridge.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
With an area of approximately , Samar is the third largest island of the Philippines, after Mindanao and Luzon. Most of Samar Island is rainforest and about a third of the island is protected by the Philippine government, as part of the Samar Island National Park. There are lots of caves in the mountains forming the island's interior, and the province of Eastern Samar has many beaches

Samar was the first island of the Philippines to be sighted by Europeans. Ferdinand Magellan, on the first circumnavigation of the world, realized that he had arrived on another archipelago since his expedition left the Mariana Islands, and sighted an island he named first as San Lázaro. Magellan did not land anywhere on the island, but on Homonhon off what is now the town of Guiuan. The present name Samar derives from samad, which means "wound" or "cut" in various Visayan languages, and dates from 1596.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
Samar was the center of one of the infamous American atrocities in the Philippine-American War. On 28 Sep 1901, U.S. Marines led by General Jacob H. Smith, led what would become known as the "March across Samar". In retaliation to Marines killed in the Balangiga encounter — which has been described in the U.S. as the worst American defeat since the Battle of Little Bighorn — Smith ordered every town and village be burnt down and every Filipino male from the age of 10 killed. Smith's orders led to condemnation from other Americans and his court-martial a year after the war ended, and the atrocities remain fresh in the consciousness of Samar residents, especially in Eastern Samar.

Formerly a single province, with the capital at Calbayog, Samar has been divided into three provinces. Most of Samar Island is sparsely populated, and rural poverty is widespread. There is also an active movement to make Samar Island its own region, in a similar fashion with the Negros Island Region. The total population of the provinces forming Samar Island totals around 2,000,000 (2015 estimate), and the majority of residents are from the Waray ethnic group.

chunks.name: Get in / By plane
chunks.text:
PAL Express flies to and from Calbayog () and Catarman (), Northern Samar to Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila or Clark International Airport in Pampanga.

Cebgo has flights to Calbayog from their Cebu hub.

Air Juan has flights to Catbalogan (no IATA) from Cebu.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text:
Major bus companies in Manila plying the Luzon-Visayas-Mindanao route pass through the province since Maharlika Highway runs through the island. Travellers to the province of Samar may ride from Metro Manila at the terminals in Cubao or Muntinlupa.

Once the bus has reached the southern tip of Luzon island, you will take a 30-minute ferryboat to the northern end of Samar, after which you can continue your bus trip, or transfer to a myriad of jeepneys, minibuses and tricycles to take you to anywhere in Samar.

chunks.name: Get in / By car
chunks.text: The western coast of Samar Island is traversed by the Asian Highway 26 route, which starts at the ferry port in Allen and continues into Leyte across the San Juanico Bridge.

chunks.name: Get around / By bus
chunks.text:
Non-AC minibuses ply the Catbalogan-Calbayog-Catarman route. There is no fixed schedule, however, and they often run full and stop at almost every barangay and small town. Due to the distances and travel times involved, they don't operate overnight, with the last departure around late afternoon.

Buses from Manila or Mindanao that ply the Maharlika Highway are available all day, however, most only stop in Calbayog and Catbalogan.

chunks.name: Get around / By van
chunks.text: Besides the buses, there are many UV Express van shuttles that ply the Catbalogan-Calbayog route almost every half an hour. These vans also ply the Calbayog-Allen and Allen-Catarman routes, with departures almost every hour. A UV from Catarman to Calbayog takes 2 hours and costs ₱100. Unlike the local buses, they run all day, yet with less frequent departures.

chunks.name: Get around / By jeepney
chunks.text: From the two urban centers of Catbalogan and Calbayog, there are jeepneys that ply from the two localities going to the various towns in the island.

chunks.name: See
chunks.text:
San Juanico Bridge between Tacloban, Leyte and Sta. Rita, Samar, is one of the longest bridges in the Philippines.
Samar Island Nature Park

chunks.name: Do
chunks.text:
The region is the caving capital of the Philippines, being home to many cave systems. Interspersed with this cave systems are waterfalls, rivers and underground rivers inside caves. Hence, the region is a destination for extreme mountaineering adventures such as spelunking and trekking.

On the Pacific coast of Eastern Samar, the island of Calicoan is home to an international surfing circuit held every year.

chunks.name: Samar Province
chunks.text: Samar, sometimes unofficially called Western Samar, is one of the three provinces in Samar Island, Eastern Visayas region of the Philippines.

chunks.name: Get in / By plane
chunks.text:

Mactan-Cebu International Airport in Metro Cebu.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text:
Major bus companies in Manila plying the Luzon-Visayas-Mindanao route pass through the province since Maharlika Highway runs through the entire length of the province. Travelers to the province of Samar may ride a bus from Metro Manila at the Ali Mall Bus Terminal in Cubao and from the various Pasay City terminals that sprout along EDSA.

Once the bus has reached the southern tip of Luzon Island, you will take a 30-minute ferryboat to the northern end of Samar, after which you can continue your bus trip, or transfer to a myriad of jeepneys, smaller buses, and tricycles to take you to anywhere in Samar.

chunks.name: Get in / By ferry
chunks.text: Cokaliong Shipping Lines: has an overnight ferry 3 times a week to/from Calbayog to Cebu city.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text:
Local mini buses ply from Catbalogan City to Tacloban City in Leyte and vice-versa and from Catbalogan to Calbayog.

On top of these buses, there are a number of passenger vans that ply Catbalogan and Calbayog route almost every half an hour. The vans also run the Catbalogan-Tacloban route almost every quarter of an hour.

Buses from Manila or Mindanao pass through the Maharlika Highway on a 24-hour basis. However, stops are only made either in Catbalogan City or Calbayog City.

From the two urban centers, Catbalogan City and Calbayog City, there are jeepneys that ply from the two localities going to the various towns of Samar.

chunks.name: See
chunks.text:
Pinipisakan Falls and Cave - San Jorge, Samar. Explore the many waterfalls and caves in the province. Pinipisakan Falls can be found in the town of San Jorge. The river in which the layers or series of waterfalls of Pinipisakan run along upstream, serves as most convenient way to enter the cave at the end of the river. Inside the cave is an underground river that serves as tributary for the Blanca Aurora river.
Langun-Gobingob Caves - Calbiga, Samar. The biggest cave system in the Philippines is the town of Calbiga. Underground rivers can also be found inside this cave system. A smaller cave system is the Kanyawa Caves also in the same town.
Lulugayan Falls. The upstream of Calbiga river is compose of many waterfalls, famous of which is the Lulugayan falls which looks like little Niagara.
Calbayog Waterfalls. The city of Calbayog boasts many waterfalls that are very accessible by motorized transport.
Samar Island Nature Park - Paranas, Samar. Commonly known as SINP, this natural park is a protected area managed by the government.

chunks.name: San Antonio (Zambales)
chunks.text:
For other cities by the name, see San Antonio (disambiguation).
San Antonio is a town of the province of Zambales in the Philippines. Situated at the western side of the mountainous Subic Peninsula, it is primarily known for its numerous secluded coves and beaches.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
San Antonio was first settled by Ilocano settlers from northern Luzon in 1830. It became an independent town in 1849. Since the American period, it has hosted Naval Station San Miguel, an annex of the US naval base in Subic Bay now run by the Philippine Navy.

The eruption of Mount Pinatubo in 1991 is credited with the town's tourism boom, as residents attributed ashfall from the volcano for filling the town's otherwise rocky beaches and coves further down the Subic Peninsula with sand and enabling groves of pine-like agujo (casuarina) trees to spring up around the coves.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
San Antonio is bypassed by the Olongapo-Bugallon Road, the main thoroughfare in Zambales. The main routes into town are two roads connecting it with the highway, one from San Marcelino and another from San Narciso.

Victory Liner buses from Metro Manila pass by the town on their way to the provincial capital, Iba and Santa Cruz. More frequent trips to San Antonio can be taken from Olongapo, where such buses make stopovers.

The main port is at Pundaquit, where fishermen can be hired to ferry tourists heading to the coves or to one-day excursions to the nearby islands.

Hiking is also a viable option for those also wanting to see the peaks of the Subic Peninsula.

chunks.name: San Dionisio
chunks.text: San Dionisio is part of Iloilo.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
By Air. Fly from Manila, Cebu, Davao and Cotabato to Iloilo Iternational Airport located in the town of Cabatuan,. Served by 10 jet flights daily from Manila that takes about an hour and Cebu for 45 minutes and 2 hours from Davao and Cotabato. The new Airport in Cabutuan which opened in the year 2007 is 19 kilometers from the city of Iloilo.
From the airport take a taxi to Bus Terminal in Tagbak, Jaro which will cost more or less 150 pesos if metered or 300 pesos more or less when fixed. One can take a taxi direct to San Dionisio (town proper) but don't pay more than 3 thousand pesos. There is also transport Vans available which cost 50 pesos to SM City.

By Land. Bus Termninal. From Tagbak, Jaro one can take either a bus or L3 van. There are direct Vans to San Dionisio but a van leaves only when it is already full of passengers. Ceres Liner has air-conditioned buses going to Estancia or Carles. There are other options from 1 stop, 2 stops or regular or other buses like HPQ in which the fares varies.
Take notice! There are no buses travelling direct to San Dionisio town proper. Pay bus fare until Sara Bus Terminal only and take the jeep in waiting going to San Dionisio (only until 5pm/ 15 pesos/person). It is advisable to take the jeep in the terminal to secure a seat. One can also get out in the crossroad of Brgy. Batuan, Sara and wait for the jeep entering the town or take a motorbike (50 pesos/bike) when carrying light baggage.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
By Sea, Take Super Ferry, Negros Navigation etc... sailing time is about 20 hours more or less from Manila; from Zamboanga or Cagayan de Oro, 14 hours twice a week; from Cebu, 12 hours once daily. There are fastcrafts Fastcrafts from Bacolod City take 50 minutes more or less. There is also a nautical highway service by Roll-on-Roll-off (RORO) vessels from various parts of the country. Bus terminals are in Ali Mall Cubao, Quezon City and Pasay City. There is a RORO bus company which has a terminal in Poblacion, San Dionisio near the public plaza.
Arriving in Iloilo City by Boat, proceed to Bus Termninal in Tagbak, Jaro or first take a sight-seeing tour in the city.
Deposit heavy luggages in SM lounge, SM City Manduriao.

chunks.name: San Fabian
chunks.text: San Fabian is a town in Pangasinan.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
San Fabian, formerly known as Angio, is one of the oldest settlements in Pangasinan, having existed in the precolonial era as a coastal trading post for Chinese, Japanese, Ilocano and Cordilleran traders. During World War II, the town was the site of amphibious landings along Lingayen Gulf by Japanese and then American forces in the battle to control Luzon. A legacy of this is its beaches being referred to by locals by the code names used by US forces who landed ashore in 1945.

San Fabian is located at the mouth of the Bued River along the northeastern shore of Lingayen Gulf, which gives the town a thriving fishing industry. It also forms Pangasinan's boundary with the province of La Union.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
San Fabian is along Route 55 (Pangasinan-La Union Road), which connects La Union with Pangasinan's commercial capital, Dagupan. Buses, jeepneys and passenger vans ply the highway, including those heading to Baguio, San Fernando and other locations further north in the Ilocos Region.

San Fabian also has direct bus connections with Metro Manila, while private vehicles take either the Binalonan or Rosario exits of the Tarlac-Pangasinan-La Union Expressway (TPLEX) and take capillary highways leading to San Fabian such as Binalonan-Dagupan Highway, which has a junction with Pangasinan-La Union Road in the town of Mangaldan to the south, or Manila North Road (MacArthur Highway), which which has a junction with Pangasinan-La Union Road in the town of Rosario to the north.

South of downtown San Fabian, in Barangay Longos, is a diversion road leading to the coastal barangays of Dagupan.

chunks.name: Get around

chunks.name: San Fernando (La Union)
chunks.text:
For other cities by the name, see San Fernando (disambiguation).
San Fernando is a city, the capital of the province of La Union in the Philippines. It is sometimes referred to with the initials of La Union's name, L.U. (as "San Fernando, L.U."), to distinguish it from the capital city of Pampanga of the same name.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: The site of San Fernando was a thriving hub for trade between Filipinos and overseas merchants from China and Japan during the precolonial era. It was then known as Pindangan, or a place for salting meat and fish. It was conquered by the Spanish in 1572 and renamed San Fernando in 1786. The town became the capital of the province of La Union upon its establishment in 1850. The town was attacked by Japanese forces during World War II due to its military bases and strategic location on a headland that juts out along the La Union coast and saw fierce fighting. It became a legally-designated city in 1998.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text: San Fernando is along Route 2 (Manila North Road). A junction at San Fernando City Plaza leads east towards the highland areas of San Fernando and the neighboring municipality of Bagulin along F. Ortega Highway.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text:
The air-con bus from Laoag to San Fernando (215 km) takes 6 hours and costs ₱330.
The air-con bus fare from San Fernando to Dau (Angeles) costs ₱300 and takes 6 hours.
There are also many buses from Metro Manila, Baguio, and Dagupan.

chunks.name: Kasay Marine Sanctuary
chunks.text: It features a 50-year-old giant clam. Formerly Wallace Air Station, this 101 hectares of base land at the end of Poro Point in San Fernando was acquired in 1903 for the United States Cavalry. It was the home of the 848th Aircraft Control and Warning Squadron which provided logistics and administrative support to other radar detachments under its chain of command. Turned over by the United States to the Republic of the Philippines on September 16, 1991, the Bases Conversion Development Authority is overseeing the plans for the conversion of the area into a prime tourism and industrial estate.

chunks.name: San Fernando (Pampanga)
chunks.text:
For other cities by the name, see San Fernando (disambiguation).
San Fernando, sometimes referred to in short as CSF or SFDO, is a city and capital of the province of Pampanga, known as the Christmas Capital of the Philippines.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
While surpassed by Angeles as the largest city and commercial center of Pampanga, San Fernando is the political, administrative, religious and cultural center of Pampanga. It is rich in culture and history, with a downtown filled with historic buildings.

San Fernando is also the "Christmas Capital of the Philippines", and every December, it holds the Giant Lantern (Parol) Festival, showcasing the handmade star-shaped Christmas lanterns created by local crafters. The city also has a Christmas-themed park, which is open all year round.

San Fernando is named after King Ferdinand II of Spain, also the patron of the city. It became the provincial capital in 1904 and a legally-designated city in 2001.

chunks.name: Get in / By car
chunks.text: San Fernando lies at a major highway crossroads; the toll North Luzon Expressway (NLEX), and national highways MacArthur Highway (Manila North Road) and Jose Abad Santos Avenue (JASA, Gapan-Olongapo Road) meet here.

chunks.name: Get in / By plane
chunks.text: The nearest airports with passenger flights are Clark International Airport () in Angeles and Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA, ) in Manila.

chunks.name: Get in / By train
chunks.text: Rail service ceased in 1988. While the tracks have long been dismantled, San Fernando's heritage station remained, and is preserved as it is the endpoint of the Bataan Death March (find at #See). The Manila-Clark Railway is under construction since 2018, and the new San Fernando station will be somewhere near the heritage station.

chunks.name: Get in / By jeep
chunks.text: San Fernando is the central hub of jeepneys from all across Pampanga, including Angeles. There are jeepneys, passenger vans and minibuses going to San Fernando from Malolos, Baliwag, Bocaue, Marilao and Meycauayan in Bulacan, and from Gapan in Nueva Ecija.

chunks.name: Metropolitan Cathedral of San Fernando

A Neoclassical church that serves as the seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of San Fernando. Originally a wooden church with a thatch roof built in 1754, it was burned by the Filipino revolutionaries under General Antonio Luna, and a Neoclassical church building was built on its place during the American era. It was again burned in 1939, and restored by the Kapampangan architect Fernando Ocampo.

chunks.name: San Gabriel (La Union)
chunks.text: San Gabriel is a town in La Union.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: San Gabriel is a landlocked municipality established along the Baroro River in the triboundary between the provinces of La Union, Ilocos Sur and Benguet. It is a highland town in the Cordillera mountains and has significant Igorot communities. Formerly a part of the Amburayan subdistrict of Mountain Province, it was annexed by La Union in 1920.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
San Gabriel is bypassed by Manila North Road (Route 2), the main thoroughfare in La Union. Instead, it is connected to the highway by roads leading to the neighboring coastal municipalities of Bacnotan and San Juan, which merge at a junction in San Gabriel between the public market and the municipal hall.

There are jeepneys connecting San Gabriel with San Juan.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: Tricycles are the main form of transportation in town.

chunks.name: Tangadan Falls
chunks.text:

address: Amontoc

chunks.name: San Jose (Batangas)
chunks.text:
For other places by the name, see San Jose.
San Jose is a rural, agricultural municipality between Lipa and Batangas City, in Batangas.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
San Jose lies between the province's two largest cities, Batangas City and Lipa. It is a common stopover for travellers on the Jose P. Laurel Highway, the major route between those locations until the Southern Tagalog Arterial Road (STAR Tollway) bypassed it. The town has many poultry farms, producing most eggs and chickens sold in Manila, so it is nicknamed the "Egg Basket of the Philippines".

The municipality used to be part of a larger municipality of Bauan, today a suburb of Batangas City. San Jose was created in 1765 as the town of San José de Malaquing Tubig, since shortened into the present name. It is named after Saint Joseph the Patriarch, its patron.

chunks.name: Get in / By jeepney
chunks.text: San Jose is served by the BN-02 jeepney route between Batangas City and Lipa. It costs around ₱30 from Batangas City bus terminal, and ₱27.5 from Lipa.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text: Frequent provincial bus services ply the highway, and they make the usual stop near the intersection at Taysan, but is hardly possible from Batangas City. A bus ticket on standard air-conditioned costs ₱135 from Pasay (1 hr, 30 min), ₱150 from Cubao (1 hr, 45 min), ₱110 from Alabang (1 hr, 15 min), and ₱70 (45 min) from Calamba.

chunks.name: Get in / By car
chunks.text:
The town lies along the highway between Lipa and Batangas City, locally called National Highway (Route 4), which bypasses the town proper to the east

STAR Tollway does not directly serve San Jose, but you can either exit at Lipa Exit or Ibaan Exit. Travel through Lipa Exit is far the most suggested, as the route via Ibaan Exit runs through forest, not best to travel through at night. A less congested route, Lodlod Avenue, also runs from Lipa, but also runs through rural and forested areas and consists of only two narrow lanes.

chunks.name: Get in / By train
chunks.text: Train service ended around the 1960s, but is proposed to be restored by the 2020s once the line between Calamba and Batangas City is rebuilt.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: Tricycles are the common transport mode through the town and surrounding area composing the larger municipality; most corners of town are reachable by tricycle.

San Jose holds a local festival in April 25, dedicated to the town's founding and its patron saint, St. Joseph the Patriarch (San Jose Patriarca).

chunks.name: San Jose (Camarines Sur)
chunks.text: San Jose is a rural municipality of 40,000 in the province of Camarines Sur in the Philippines

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
The town of San Jose, then known as Danlog, was a barrio of nearby Lagonoy in the early 19th century. It remained part of Lagonoy until the year 1813 when San Jose was established under the name of Patrocinio derived from the Spanish word patrón which means "model". Later, the words de San José were attached to its former name, thus becoming Patrocinio de San José. It was soon shortened to San Jose which is now the official name of the municipality.

May 19 marks the annual celebration of the feast day of San Jose (st. Joseph), the town's patron saint.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text:
From Naga: Take any bus from the central terminal and headed for Lagonoy. The bus will pass through the towns of Pili, Ocampo, Tigaon and Goa and finally bring the visitor after 1½-2 hr to San Jose. Alternatively, you can take a van, which takes 1-1½ hr.

From Legazpi: take a bus to Naga, then follow the directions above. For a more scenic route via Tabaco, take a bus or van around the spectacular Mount Mayon to Tabaco then transfer to Goa. This route provides breathtaking scenery as it meanders along the jagged coastline with views out to Ataluyan Island and Caramoan Peninsula.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: Vans and buses frequently travel between San Jose, Goa and Naga from Lagonoy or Sabang port. Within San Jose, jeepneys regularly run to Sabang port and tricycles and padyaks (non-motorized tricycles) are very popular.

chunks.name: Sabang Beach
chunks.text:
The coastal tip of San Jose's shorelines, frequented by tourists and travellers bound to Caramoan Peninsula.
address: Sabang, San Jose, Camarines Sur

chunks.text:

Adiangao Cave - located in Adiangao San Jose, the entrance to this cave is on the side of a small hill overlooking the sea.
Tagithi Falls is almost 2 hours away from Adiangao proper.
Pamaypay Falls- known as Abaniko Falls, in English - Fan Falls, located approximately 1 km from Barangay Adiangao. The falls is near Barangay Ayugao.
Libtong Falls - 50 m away from Adiangao. This is the favourite swimming area of the children of Adingao
Cawa Falls - called Cawa because the falls looks like a big cooking pot.

chunks.name: Do
chunks.text: San Jose is surrounded with beautiful mountains, rivers, beaches and waterfalls. It is set amongst rice paddocks and the visitor must be prepared to explore to fully enjoy what the area has to offer.

chunks.name: Eat
chunks.text: San Jose has a well known Mamihan noodle soup which is just around the Centro of San Jose a Mamihan called "Kino" offers great taste of Mami that will surely full your stomach.

chunks.name: Sleep
chunks.text: San Jose has homestay and resort accommodation options for those wishing to stay a while and relax on its beaches, or for those wishing to overnight on their way to Caramoan. The easternmost barangay of Adiangao has beautiful limestone cliffs set up in the hills over looking the ocean and town proper. This is reached by boat from Sabang or Dolo port after 45 minutes.

chunks.name: San Jose (Mindoro)
chunks.text: San Jose is a municipality in Occidental Mindoro, Philippines. San Jose offers an off-the-beaten-path charm for tourists who shun the crowded and over-commercialized spots in the country. The major attractions of San Jose are its three offshore islands - Ambulong, Ilin, and White Island (also called Manadi). San Jose is also a favorite jump-off point to the world-class diving site - Apo Reef Marine Park.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
Even with its considerable tourism potential, San Jose has yet to turn into a more popular destination at par with other parts of the Philippines. Among the challenges the town faces are coastal pollution, illegal settlers, and a lack of an effective ecotourism plan. Brownouts caused by a lingering power supply dispute have negatively affected local businesses and tourism.

However, a modest number of visitors continue to explore this quaint town on the southwestern tip of Mindoro.

chunks.name: San Jose Airport
chunks.text: With regular scheduled flights from Manila by Cebu Pacific. Flights take approximately 30 minutes from Manila.

chunks.name: Get in / By land
chunks.text:
RORO Bus, and Philtranco have direct bus routes from Cubao in Quezon City, Sampaloc in Manila and Alabang in Muntinlupa) to San Jose that includes a roll-on/roll-off (RORO) ferry that operates between Batangas City and the port at Abra de Ilog. The ferry passes through Verde Island Passage and takes about three hours.

San Jose is linked to all towns of Occidental Mindoro via a mostly-dusty provincial highway that runs from north to south. Roads in and around San Jose are well-paved on mostly flat terrain. Local bus and jeepney operators ply the route from the northernmost town of Abra de Ilog all the way south to San Jose.

Vans run from the bus terminal all the way to Calapan (6 hr, ₱500) along the eastern coast of Mindoro.

chunks.name: Get in / By sea
chunks.text: has boats to and from Coron three times a week (₱800, 8 hr). You can book tickets or find out about the schedule on biyaheroes.com.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text:
Most roads in the Poblacion area and nearby barangays are either paved with concrete or asphalt. The major thoroughfares are Rizal Street, Liboro Street, Bonifacio Street, Mabini Street, and the streets in and around the public market. Motored tricycles are the common mode of transportation around town. Jeepneys provide the main mode of public transportation between San Jose and other towns of the province.
Pump boats can be chartered to provide access to nearby island resorts and diving spots.

chunks.name: Ambulong Island
chunks.text: Ambulong Island is a 30-km² island with fine beaches, cliffs and abundant coral formations. It is characterized by white sand beaches, cliffs along pillars jutting out of the water, and underwater caves. Coral gardens and tropical fish are abundant in several coves. An islet called Grace Island is located at a limestone cove at the southern tip of Ambulong. A fisherman's village is located at the sheltered side of the island. Ambulong Island is also a jump-off point to some of the dive spots in the area, such as the Iling Point, Baniaga Reef, Ambulong Bank, Dungan Reef, Sardines Reef, Apo Reef, and Manadi Island. These dive sites are about an hour away by pumpboat from the Caminawit Port.

chunks.name: Ilin Island
chunks.text: Ilin Island has a village of shell divers, being abundant in shells and coral reefs. There are ancient burial caves of early Chinese traders, ethnic fishing villages, and numerous dive sites from which to view many tropical fishes. Lush foliage encircle the clear blue waters of the South China Sea. There are scuba diving facilities, a 6.8 CTM compressor, seaport facilities, diveboats, and PADI and NAUI-certified instructors. Kweba Cansubong is a popular destination in the island apart from its white beaches, estuaries, rock formations, etc. Inasakan Beach, located at the far side of Ilin, is a small stretch of powdery white sand. It has been proposed to declare the island's timberland a conservation area for its natural fauna and flora. The Philippine teak, an endangered Philippine tree, is found only in Ilin and Batangas. Meanwhile, an endangered fauna called the cloud rat (or cloud runner/Ilin Island cloud runner) is found only in San Jose, Occidental Mindoro particularly in the island of Ilin. The cloud rat is the biggest and one of the most beautiful rats in the world.

chunks.name: White Island
chunks.text: White Island has a long powdery beach where buried turtle eggs are occasionally found. It has an almost mile-long beach with smooth and powdery white sand. The tranquil and peaceful island is an ideal place for swimming, scuba diving and fishing. Turtle eggs are occasionally found buried in the sand, and visitors are cautioned to keep them undisturbed.

Cultural events in San Jose include Indak Pandurukan, a street-dancing festival, and other activities during the town fiesta which is celebrated on May 1.

chunks.name: Mt. Iglit National Park
chunks.text: Mounts Iglit-Baco National Park is located in an area shared by the municipalities of Sablayan, Calintaan, Rizal and San Jose. The latter is also the main gateway there. It is a sanctuary for the 'tamaraw' (Bubalus mindorensis), an endemic species of buffalo found only in Mindoro. It provides a nice eco-tourism, trekking, or mountaineering alternative to beach/dive resorts. However, a part of the tamaraw genepool which is also a part of the national park is at the boundaries of Rizal and San Jose, more or less 50 hectares are in the territorial jurisdiction of the municipality.

chunks.name: San Jose (Nueva Ecija)
chunks.text:
For other places by the name, see San Jose.
San Jose, often called San Jose City or SJC in short, is a small city in Nueva Ecija.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
San Jose sits at the foot of the Caraballo Mountains that forms the boundary with Nueva Vizcaya. It is at the crossroads of three highways, the Maharlika Highway (Route 1) which connects Metro Manila with Nueva Vizcaya and Cagayan Valley, San Jose-Lupao Road (Route 56) which leads to Pangasinan, and Rizal-San Jose Road (Route 111) which leads to Aurora.

The city used to be the barrio of Cabaritan (Kabaritan) in nearby Lupao until the Spaniards decided to upgrade it to a town in 1894 and renamed it after its patron saint, St. Joseph. It is the commercial center of northern Nueva Ecija, and forms one of the three metropolitan areas of the province, alongside Cabanatuan and Gapan.

. Agriculture is the main source of local revenue, and around the city are sprawling rice paddies which dominate the landscape.

chunks.name: Get in

chunks.text: San Jose is a city in Palawan, Philippines.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text: Buses arrive from Puerto Princesa, Sabang and El Nido. Only the bus from Puerto Princesa goes all the way to Port Barton, so if you're coming from somewhere else and going to Port Barton, you'll have change buses here. Going to Port Barton, you can either wait for the bus from Puerto Princesa or hire a motorcycle to take you the rest of the way to Port Barton. The bus is much cheaper but only runs when there are enough passenger boarding in Puerto Princesa, so you might have to hire a motorcycle.

chunks.name: San Jose de Buenavista
chunks.text: San Jose de Buenavista, or simply San Jose, is a town of 63,000 and the capital of Antique province in the Philippines, on Panay island.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
The first people who lived around San Jose are the indigenous Ati, or Negritos, until one of the ten datus who left Borneo and settled in Panay bought their traditional lands along the coast. What would become San Jose started as the village of Tubigon ("under water" in the Kinaray-a language), then a part of nearby Hamtic, mostly covered by jungle and was frequently targeted by Moro pirates. Tubigon became a formal settlement in 1733, and its first parish church was established in 1790. The center of government is at the sitio (hamlet) of Mala-iba, soon renamed to San Jose, both after its patron saint and the son of a local town chief. When Antique is separated from Oton (present Iloilo province), San Jose is made the capital, but only in 1872 became a town and the suffix "de Buenavista" was added after its remarkable views.

San Jose is from Iloilo City, but it receives few visitors. One draw to San Jose is the Binirayan Festival, the beaches and the town. The pace of life in San Jose is much relaxed, and there are few visitors.

The circumstances behind Javier's assassination remains unknown, but he is known for his vocal opposition to president Ferdinand Marcos.

chunks.name: San Jose del Monte
chunks.text: San Jose del Monte City, also known by its initials SJDM, is the largest city in Bulacan by population. A suburb of Metro Manila, it may look gritty at times, but has its own attractions and resorts.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
SJDM was founded in the 18th century and was little more than a provincial town. This changed in the 1980s, when thousands of informal settlers from Metro Manila were relocated to San Jose del Monte. The city is home to some of the biggest resettlement areas in the Philippines like the Sapang Palay resettlement area spread over 36 barangays, Pabahay 2000 in Barangay Muzon and Towerville in Barangay Minuyan Proper. Most of the city's population come from former informal settlers along the creeks, esteros, riverbanks and railway tracks of Metro Manila. Since then, the city is gradually becoming integrated with the urban sprawl originating from the national capital, and is now directly connected with it through public transportation.

There have been growing demands for SJDM to become a highly-urbanized city administratively independent from Bulacan; this has consistently been opposed by the provincial government, which fears a loss of important revenue once this happens.

chunks.text: San Jose del Monte is 65 kilometres (40 mi) from Malolos and 30 kilometres (19 mi) from Manila.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text: There are many city buses heading to San Jose del Monte from Metro Manila, mostly via Quirino Highway. The most common route to San Jose del Monte is the PITX-Grotto route, which plies Manila, Commonwealth Avenue, and Quirino Avenue.

chunks.name: Get in / By jeepney
chunks.text: There are many jeepneys and minibuses heading to San Jose del Monte from Metro Manila, mainly from SM Fairview in Quezon City via Quirino Highway. There are also connections with neighboring towns and cities of Bulacan such as Meycauayan, Norzagaray and Santa Maria.

chunks.name: Get in / By taxi
chunks.text: Taxis (both car and motorcycle) and Grab can also be used to access areas of SJDM directly bordering Metro Manila.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: The sheer size and number of barangays in SJDM has resulted in multiple intracity routes plied by jeepneys and minibuses.

The site also covers parts of the towns of Doña Remedios Trinidad, Angat, San Rafael, and San Miguel, as well as parts of Rizal, Quezon, Aurora and Nueva Ecija provinces.

chunks.text:
For other places by the name, see San Juan (disambiguation).
San Juan is a municipality of Batangas. It is home to the other beaches in the province besides those in the west coast and Mabini;

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: San Juan is composed of a Spanish-era town center (poblacion) with streets laid out in a grid, and a larger area mostly agricultural in background. The town is at the center of the main route between Batangas and Quezon provinces. A major tourist draw is the white-sand beaches of Laiya, to the south of town; today, tourism is a major local source of revenue, after aquaculture and agriculture.

chunks.name: ALPS Bus Terminal
chunks.text: address: General Luna Street, Poblacion

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
San Juan is served by some bus companies:

ALPS the Bus has trips from their Manila terminals to the downtown.
Supreme has service from Batangas City to Lucena through these town, using a mix of air-conditioned and ordinary buses.
P&O runs Batangas City-Tagkawayan using an air-conditioned fleet. No advanced booking is needed for short to medium distances, e.g. from Batangas City or Lucena, but a pre-booked ticket is necessary if coming from their Tagkawayan terminal.

A trip from Batangas City by bus costs at around ₱84 to downtown (₱74 from Lucena terminal).

Jeepneys are a cheaper option, but are uncomfortable and infrequent outside daylight hours. Nonetheless, they are the only public transport option from Lipa. From Batangas City, a jeepney trip will entail a transfer at downtown Rosario, west, which can be only a waste of time and money, and jeepneys from there are infrequent. Better catch a bus from the Grand Terminal.

By car, the Rosario-San Juan-Candelaria Road and the Quezon Eco-tourism Road are the main highways to town. The Rosario-San Juan leg of the former and the whole segment of the latter forms Route 422; they provide the best road connection from Lucena, but the coastal portion can look a bit isolated, as it passes through coastal villages through the municipalities of Sariaya and Candelaria. Marcial C. Punzalan Jr. Highway leads to a junction with the Maharlika Highway in Tiaong, Quezon.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text:
The town center at the barangay of Poblacion is compact, and walkable. Tricycles are abundant.

There is a highway between Poblacion and Laiya. There are many improvements along the road, including widened bridges and added lanes. Car travel is advisable but not necessary.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: San Juan was founded by the Spanish in 1772. It was originally known as Lapog, after a local word for bamboo. It was renamed after its patron saint in 1961. The town is known as the "Buri Capital of Ilocos Sur" for its production of handicrafts made from the buri palm (Corypha utan).

The nearest cruise ship terminal is in Salomague Port in neighboring Cabugao, 10 km to the north.

chunks.name: San Juan (La Union)
chunks.text:
For other places by the name, see San Juan (disambiguation).
San Juan is a town in La Union.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
The town was founded by the Spanish in 1586. Long dismissed as a quiet agrarian suburb of San Fernando, it began attracting tourists from Metro Manila in the 2000s for its surfing-worthy waves and viability for a day-trip to and from Baguio. There is not much to see and to do here for an average tourist, except surfing. The two most touristic areas are both some kilometers outside of San Juan:

Urbiztondo There are several resorts in this area with rooms, restaurants and surf lessons. Resorts are quite pricey. Prices for surfboards are usually about ₱200 per hour, surf lessons also amount to ₱200 per hour (Feb 2010). The swell is usually slightly better than in Montemar. The water can get very crowded, especially on weekends where you may count more than 70 surfers along the short beach.
Montemar Is less developed, fewer resorts and you have all the water for yourself. Bring your own board or choose one of the resorts that rent out boards. Resorts do cost less here on average compared to Urbiztondo. Prices for boards are about ₱120 per hour. Surf lessons are not available here.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
San Juan is along Route 2 (Manila North Road). The best way to get here is by bus from Manila. Take one of the many bus lines bound to La Union, Ilocos Sur or Ilocos Norte. Tell the bus driver to drop you at San Juan - Sebay (Urbiztondo) or San Juan - Montemar. Both are well known stops among the bus drivers. Downtown San Juan is your typical provincial commercial center and has nothing to offer related to surfing.

A junction in Barangay Ili Norte in downtown San Juan leads east towards the municipality of San Gabriel.

chunks.text: Tricycles are the main form of public transportation around town.

Experienced surfers used to Hawaiian swells will yawn but San Juan has a reliable swell that is great for beginners and intermediates. Surfing Season is from November to April with reliable waves until end of January. Later there may be week-long periods without even the most minimal swell.

chunks.name: San Juan (Metro Manila)
chunks.text: San Juan is a small city in Metro Manila, surrounded by Manila, Mandaluyong and Quezon City.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
It used to be a large municipality, this little city is sandwiched between the cities of Mandaluyong, Manila and Quezon City. It has a population of about 120,000 as of 2015, and a total land area of .

San Juan is a young city, only chartered in 2007. It used to be the town of San Juan del Monte, after its patron John the Baptist, and for its hilly terrain, and is the site of one major battle of the Philippine Revolution, the Battle of San Juan del Monte (more known locally as the Battle of Pinaglabanan).

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text:
The city proper is served by city bus route 2 between Quiapo, Manila and Taytay, Rizal. The route plies San Juan's main roads, N. Domingo St and Ortigas Ave.

If coming from southern Metro Manila, take the MRT Line 3 or EDSA Carousel and get down at Ortigas station, then walk to Robinsons Galleria at the intersection of EDSA and Ortigas Ave where you can ride the route 2 bus or a jeepney.

chunks.name: Get in / By jeepney
chunks.text: Jeepneys from various terminals near the Agora market are bound for Divisoria in Manila, Arayat Market in Cubao, Camp Crame, Kalentong near the city's border with Mandaluyong, and Rosario in Pasig, which passes through Greenhills.

chunks.name: J. Ruiz station
chunks.text:
Served by LRT Line 2, it is the only rapid transit station in the city, but is at an impractical location above Aurora Boulevard. It is poorly connected to local public transportation (except for jeepneys plying Aurora Boulevard), and to reach the downtown means a walk through a somewhat seedy area.
address: Aurora Blvd, Salapan

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text:
The city is small enough to be explored by cycling, and neighborhood districts are walkable. It is also possible to get around by tricycle or jeepney.

There are available jeepneys in Agora Market that are bound for Little Baguio.

chunks.name: San Luis (Batangas)
chunks.text: San Luis is a municipality, including the town of San Luis and some rural areas, south of Taal in Batangas. . Its main attraction is beaches.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
The town is typical for the Philippines with a lovely Catholic church, a market, quite a few carinderias serving cheap Philippine food, and not much else.

Outside town there are a number of beach resorts with the usual amenities. Most have boats available for diving trips out to nearby reefs. There is also one public beach where you can swim without paying a resort entry fee.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
There are two highways to San Luis. The usual route is along the coast from Taal or Lemery either by jeepney or car. That highway is short and in good shape; traffic is rarely horrible but often heavy enough to be somewhat annoying. Beyond San Luis it continues south to Balite.

The other highway leads inland to Bauan where it connects to the main highway between Lemery and Batangas City; if you are coming from Batangas, this is the shortest route. That highway is two-lane blacktop, mostly good but with a few rough patches, does not wind much, and generally carries only light traffic.

chunks.name: San Luis (Pampanga)
chunks.text:
For other places by the name, see San Luis.
San Luis is a town in Pampanga, Philippines. It is a quiet agricultural town bypassed by the province's major highways.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: Formerly known as San Nicolas de Cabagsac, San Luis was established along a bend of the Pampanga River and the southern edge of the Candaba Swamp in 1742. It was renamed and rededicated in honor of Saint Aloysius Gonzaga. It is a generally quiet town reliant on agriculture, particularly rice farming, with a few upheavals throughout its history such as peasant revolts, World War II guerrillas and the Huk Rebellion, led by its native son Luis Taruc.

chunks.name: Saint Aloysius Transport Cooperative
chunks.text:
The main jeepney terminal in San Luis occupies a makeshift row of tarpaulins along the front fence of San Luis Elementary School.
address: Santa Cruz Poblacion

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
San Luis is bypassed by the major highways of Pampanga. From Manila, take the San Fernando exit along the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) leading to the Gapan-Olongapo Road, also known as Jose Abad Santos Avenue (JASA). From NLEX, go east towards Mexico, then take the Santo Domingo Circle with signage pointing to San Luis. A road built over the Arnedo Dike also connects San Luis to other towns of eastern Pampanga such as San Simon and its eponymous exit along NLEX, Apalit, Candaba and Arayat. A secondary road connects the city of Baliwag in Bulacan province.

From Robinsons Starmills in the provincial capital San Fernando, there is a jeepney heading to San Luis, but as these run in irregular intervals due to the practice of waiting for the vehicle to fill up at the terminal, many commuters take jeepneys heading to Arayat and then disembark at Santo Domingo Circle before taking a tricycle to San Luis instead. A one-way solo trip by trike costs P90.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: Downtown San Luis is compact and easily accessible on foot. Tricycles are the main form of transportation between barangays.

chunks.name: San Luis Gonzaga Parish Church
chunks.text:
San Luis's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a mix of Baroque and Renaissance styles. The turreted and unplastered brick façade itself is unlike the typical flat church exterior found elsewhere.
address: Santa Cruz Poblacion

chunks.name: Luis Taruc Monument
chunks.text:
Placed on a road junction next to the municipal park, it is memorial depicting a sculpture of a peasant family. It is dedicated to the town's most famous resident, Luis Taruc, a peasant leader who founded the Hukbalahap, the country's largest guerrilla organization fighting against the Japanese in World War II, and then the Philippine government when it reneged on its promises to grant land reform after independence in 1946. Taruc surrendered in 1954, but dissenters within the movement regrouped themselves into the New People's Army in 1968, continuing one of the world's longest leftwing insurgencies. Taruc himself was imprisoned but was eventually amnestied and rehabilitated before dying in 2005 aged 92. Taruc's ashes are interred at the base of the monument.
address: Bahay Pare Road, Santo Tomas

chunks.name: Hukbalahap Monument
chunks.text:
A monument built in 2023 at the entrance of a private cemetery to honor the Hukbalahap (an abbreviation of Hukbong Bayan Laban sa Hapon; translated as People's Anti-Japanese Army) movement founded by Luis Taruc, who was born in what was then the rural village of Santa Monica in 1913. It features concrete statues depicting Taruc and two of his comrades in the Huk movement. Its construction, along with that of Taruc's solo monument in the downtown, marks the rehabilitation of the Huks as agrarian nationalist heroes after being vilified for decades as communist bogeymen in the political paranoia caused by the Cold War.
address: Provincial Road, Santa Monica

chunks.name: Old San Luis Bridge Park
chunks.text:
A recreational space built over the remaining span of the old bridge over the Pampanga River connecting downtown San Luis with its rural barangays.
address: Provincial Road, Santo Tomas

While still risky, these rats are relatively safer to eat than their urban counterparts as they live on a somewhat "organic" diet in the farm.

chunks.name: San Mateo (Rizal)
chunks.text:
For other cities by the name, see San Mateo.
San Mateo is a town in Rizal, Philippines. It is considered the gateway to the northern part of the province.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: Founded by the Augustinians in the 16th century, the town was named after a town in Spain due to its geographical resemblance, in which the town is near a high mountain and has a river that flowed through its center, which often floods but quickly recedes. , and is part of the urban sprawl extending northeast from Metro Manila along the Marikina River.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
San Mateo is 24 km away from Manila and 11 km away from Antipolo. It is accessible via J.P. Rizal from Marikina and Batasan-San Mateo Road in Quezon City. San Mateo and Rodriguez are accessible to the rest of Rizal via Marikina.

Jeepneys and UVs pass by the town via Gen. Luna Ave. and Mabini Ave. A jeepney fare from Quezon City Hall costs P28.

There are a couple of jeepney terminals in Silangan that are bound for Cubao, passing through Fortune in Marikina. The route of those terminals have some passages different from each other.

Taxis (both car and motorcycle) and Grab can also be used to access areas of San Mateo directly bordering Metro Manila.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: Places along the main roads are accessible by jeepneys. Places within villages are accessible by tricycles served in their designated places and cars. Pintong Bukawe, the town's easternmost barangay, is only accessible by passing through Cabading in Antipolo.

chunks.name: San Miguel (Bulacan)
chunks.text:
For other places by the name, see San Miguel.
San Miguel is a municipality in the province of Bulacan, Philippines. A rural town in the middle of the Central Luzon plains, it counts heritage structures, extensive national parks and dairy-based candy-makers among its tourist draws.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
San Miguel was founded during the Spanish era and was originally known as San Miguel de Mayumo, Mayumo being a Kapampangan term for "sweet". Originally a barrio of Candaba, the town passed back and forth between Pampanga, Nueva Ecija and Bulacan before finally being claimed by the latter province. In 1897, the mountains east of town became the headquarters of the Biaknabato Republic, a protostate of the Philippine revolutionary government led by president Emilio Aguinaldo that lasted until the signing of a ceasefire agreement with the Spanish in November that year.

In the early 20th century, San Miguel became a fashionable spa town for its natural springs such as Sibul, which has since dried up thanks to mining activities. Despite this, there are significant natural attractions remaining in town, with Aguinaldo’s mountain hideout in Biaknabato being declared a national park in 1937.

. It is the third largest municipality by area in the province after Doña Remedios Trinidad, which was partially carved out of San Miguel, and Norzagaray. It forms the tripoint boundary between the provinces of Bulacan, Pampanga and Nueva Ecija.

chunks.name: Baliwag Transit
chunks.text: address: Norberto Street, Tigpalas

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
San Miguel lies along Maharlika Highway, also known as Asian Highway 26 (AH 26) and Cagayan Valley Road. From Metro Manila, it is served by buses heading to the neighboring city of Gapan and Cabanatuan in Nueva Ecija. Jeepneys also running between Gapan and Tabang in Plaridel, just off the Santa Rita Exit of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) leading to Maharlika Highway, also pass through San Miguel.

Baliwag Transit and its sister company, Golden Bee, have a dedicated bus terminal in San Miguel.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: Tricycles are the main form of transportation between barangays, especially as Maharlika Highway skirts the western edges of downtown San Miguel. Fares start at P40.

chunks.name: San Miguel Arcangel Church
chunks.text:
San Miguel's main Roman Catholic church, built during the 19th century and used as a garrison by opposing sides during the Philippine Revolution against Spain. It houses a statue of Saint Michael the Archangel that was found in the forests outside town and is believed by residents to be miraculous. It is one of a few churches in the Philippines whose belfry is built above its façade. There is a souvenir shop in the convent.
address: Libertad Street, Poblacion

chunks.name: Biak-na-Bato National Park
chunks.text:
A sprawling 2117 ha national park that also covers parts of the neighboring towns of Doña Remedios Trinidad and San Ildefonso. Famous as the site of the Biak-na-Bato Republic during the Philippine Revolution, it also contains caves, rivers and forested highlands of the Sierra Madre that belie the misconception of Bulacan as a largely flat province.
address: Magsaysay Road, Biak-na-Bato

chunks.name: Banal na Bundok
chunks.text:
Meaning "Holy Mountain" in Filipino, it is a hillside monument/park filled with monuments to Jesus Christ and other key figures in the Bible. It is a popular pilgrimage site during the Lenten season, when visitors clamber to pray atop the various hilltop shrines.
address: Sibul-Biaknabato Road, Sitio Pangarayuman, Barangay Biak na Bato

chunks.name: Mount Manalmon
chunks.text:
A 196 m peak that is popular among hikers in Biak-na-Bato National Park. It also contains Madlum Cave and forms one side of a gorge along the Madlum River that is also shared with Mount Gola, another popular hiking destination. The area is also claimed by the municipality of Doña Remedios Trinidad.
address: Kamias

chunks.text:
A residence built for the Tecson family, whose members included an officer in the Philippine Revolution.
address: Rizal Street

chunks.name: Sevilla House

A now decrepit residence built in 1921 for a former mayor. Unlike other houses at the time, the dwelling has three storeys.
address: Tecson Street

chunks.text: San Miguel contains a considerable number of colonial-era residences whose conditions range from decrepit to still inhabited and preserved by its original owners. These are mostly concentrated in Poblacion, particularly in Rizal and Tecson Streets.

chunks.name: San Pablo (Laguna)
chunks.text:
For other places by the name, see San Pablo (disambiguation).
San Pablo is a city in the province of Laguna, known for its seven lakes.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: Having existed since pre-colonial times, San Pablo passed back and forth between Laguna and Batangas before becoming firmly part of the former province during the Spanish era. Its fertile volcanic soil proved beneficial for coconut farming, resulting in the entry of large corporations such as Franklin Baker during the American period. Due to its rapid economic development, San Pablo received its city charter in 1940, making it one of the oldest legally-designated cities in the Philippines. . Since 1967, it has also been the seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of San Pablo, placing it at the heart of the Roman Catholic church in Laguna.

chunks.name: Understand / Orientation
chunks.text:
San Pablo is a compact city that lies at the junction of the Maharlika Highway and to other major cities in Laguna and Quezon. It was also a major stop on the Philippine National Railways from Manila to Lucena and is expected to be so again once the railway reopens following rehabilitation works.

Unlike the other major cities of Laguna, which are located along Laguna de Bay's flatlands, San Pablo has a relatively cooler climate on account of its higher elevation, forested surroundings and seven lakes. It is also surrounded on nearly all sides by volcanic mountains and hills that form the Laguna Volcanic Field. On a clear day, it is possible to obtain panoramic views of Mount Makiling, Mount San Cristobal, Mount Banahaw, Mount Manabu and Mount Kalisungan.

chunks.name: Understand / Orientation
chunks.text: Downtown San Pablo lies at the southern shore of Sampaloc Lake, the largest of the city's seven lakes. The city hall and other civic buildings lie near the promontory leading down to the lake, while the town plaza and San Pablo Cathedral are located shortly to the south. The main thoroughfare is Jose Rizal Avenue, a four-lane boulevard that runs east to west and around which jeepney terminals, heritage buildings and commercial buildings congregate. At its eastern edge sits San Pablo Cathedral and Plaza Rizal, a key junction. Werner Schetelig Avenue leads northeast towards towns at the slope of Mount Banahaw such as Nagcarlan, Liliw, Majayjay and Lucban, Quezon while further west, Rizal Avenue becomes Colago Avenue and meets with Cosigo Avenue leading to Calauan and the rest of Laguna before merging with Maharlika Highway leading to Batangas and Manila. South of the Plaza, a road leads to Maharlika Highway for those heading to Tiaong and the rest of Quezon Province.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text: From Manila, the fastest route by road is through the STAR Tollway exiting at Santo Tomas exit in Batangas, from there, enter the Maharlika Highway and follow the road signs leading to Alaminos and then San Pablo.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text: Bus companies running frequent services between Manila and Lucena stop at San Pablo, as well as some of those from Bicol and the interisland buses. Designated stops are at the Central Terminal, SM City San Pablo, San Rafael (near the junction of Maharlika Highway and Cipriano Colago Avenue) and at Franklin Baker (between railroad crossing and Unson Street at San Anton and Ambray), all along the highway.

chunks.name: Get in / By car
chunks.text:
Maharlika Highway (Asian Highway 26/Route 1) is the main highway through San Pablo, along with the Calauan-San Pablo Road (Route 67). It is from Manila, from Lucena, and from Los Baños.

Construction is continuing for an extension of the South Luzon Expressway to Lucena, with an exit in San Pablo.

chunks.name: Get in / By jeepney
chunks.text: Jeepneys connect San Pablo with the nearby towns of Alaminos, Calauan, Rizal, Dolores, and Tiaong, and travel as far as Liliw via Rizal and Nagcarlan on Werner Schetelig Avenue, Santa Cruz via Calauan, Tanauan (in Batangas) and Calamba via Bay. Only the routes from Tanauan, Calamba, Santa Cruz, and Liliw are run by licensed vehicles, with the route from Dolores run by unmarked and unlicensed vehicles with private vehicle license plates. Terminals are at the city proper or at SM City San Pablo.

chunks.name: San Pablo station
chunks.text: Served by the Bicol Express and Mayon Limited (both suspended since 2015). Unloading only for northbound trains. There is also a regional service to San Pablo from Lucena and Calamba.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text:
Tricycles and jeepneys running from the city center to outlying barangays are the main form of transport within the city.

Downtown and the Maharlika Highway can get very congested during rush hour. During the holidays, queues of vehicles entering the STAR Tollway in Batangas heading to Manila can reach San Pablo.

chunks.name: Komikero Komiks Museum
chunks.text:
A museum dedicated to comic strips featuring the collection of comic artist Gerry Alanguilan, whose works include domestic and international publications such as Marvel and DC Comics.
hours: Mon-Fri 1-5 PM by appointment; address: 29 Marasigan St., cor Azcarate Circle

chunks.name: Lake Sampaloc
chunks.text: The largest of San Pablo's seven lakes, of volcanic origin. Around the lake are Dagatan Boulevard, a lakefront park, floating cottages, and various civic monuments such as that of a giant tilapia fish.

chunks.name: Saint Paul the First Hermit Cathedral
chunks.text:
An adobe Romanesque Roman Catholic cathedral that forms the center of San Pablo and serves as the seat of the namesake Roman Catholic Diocese of San Pablo which oversees the entirety of Laguna. Built in 1714, it was damaged during World War II, and its façade been restored to its original. Its dome is a landmark of the city.
address: A. Flores Street, Poblacion

chunks.name: Doña Leonila Park
chunks.text:
A tree-filled park filled with fountains and neoclassical and Filipino-themed statues, it is a favorite recreation hub among residents. It sits on a promontory overlooking Dagatan Boulevard and provides views of Sampaloc Lake.
address: Trece Martires Street co. Dagatan Boulevard

chunks.name: Trece Martires Shrine
chunks.text: address: Trece Martires Street

chunks.name: Andres Bonifacio Monument
chunks.text: address: Trece Martires Street

chunks.name: Fule-Malvar Mansion
chunks.text:
A prominent landmark, the mansion was built in 1915 in the beaux-arts and Art Nouveau style that was typical of the American period for the first city mayor of San Pablo, Potenciano Malvar, and his wife, Eusebia Fule, both of which came from prominent families. Visiting presidents and dignitaries were often hosted here. Since then the house has changed ownership multiple times and as of 2025 is being used as a civic center by the city government.
address: Jose Rizal Avenue

chunks.name: Doña Prudencia D. Fule Ancestral House
chunks.text:
A Spanish-era bahay na bato last inhabited by a scion of the Fule family known for her devotion to the education sector. In the 1930s, she donated the house and the adjoining plot to build a high school that now bears her name. The house was at times used as a school building before falling into neglect and becoming inhabited by squatters claiming to be Doña Prudencia's heirs. Following a legal battle to remove aforementioned squatters, the house was restored in 2019 and now contains a school museum. On the other side of the highway, at the elementary school also named after Prudencia, is one of the few Gabaldon school bungalows in the Philippines that dates back to the American period.

To avoid confusion with the Fule-Malvar Mansion, Prudencia is located outside downtown, on the highway running between the city and Alaminos, and is painted in strips of ocean-green and white with a red roof.
hours: Museum for Industrial Arts and Economics: Open Mon-Fri during school hours. Otherwise ask caretakers for permission.; address: Prudencia D. Fule Memorial National High School, Maharlika Highway, Brgy. San Nicolas

chunks.name: Old San Pablo City Hall
chunks.text:
Built in a neo-classical style, this imposing structure is one of the few surviving civic buildings in the Philippines from the pre-World War II era. It contains a small museum on the history of San Pablo.
hours: Mon-Fri 8AM-5PM; address: Capitol Compound, Trece Martirez Street

chunks.name: Pio Conducto Ancestral House
chunks.text:
A private residence built for one of San Pablo's well-to-do residents in 1924, it became known as the setting of the 1988 classic Filipino horror film Tiyanak featuring a demon-baby from Filipino folklore and has since become a stereotype for a haunted house, lightened somewhat by the grotto of the Virgin Mary in the yard. Only the semi-cylindrical exterior and ornate window grills can be seen on the outside, but if one is lucky enough to be invited in, expect to see the interior of an American period house complete with custom-made furniture from that era. There are plans to restore the house, which has not been directly inhabited by its owners for some time, to its former glory.
address: 126 Werner Schetelig Avenue, Barangay III-E

chunks.name: Twin Lakes
chunks.text: Two of San Pablo's Seven Crater Lakes, situated in close proximity to each other and separated only by a narrow isthmus. These lakes are the most suitable among the seven for recreational activities, including swimming, and offer pristine unspoiled waters. There are camping accommodations nearby.

chunks.name: Mount San Cristobal
chunks.text: A towering 1470 m inactive volcano east of San Pablo, along the boundary with Quezon province. Situated alongside Mount Banahaw, a religious pilgrimage site, it is said to be the mountain's "evil twin", having been dubbed the "Devil's Mountain" for malevolent entities said to inhabit its slopes.

chunks.name: See
chunks.text: Unlike other cities in the Philippines with a similar population, San Pablo retains a sizeable number of heritage buildings, mostly dating from the American period. Many of them are concentrated along the Capital Compound, Plaza Rizal and along Jose Rizal Avenue, which retains its original lamp posts, traffic islands and colonnaded footbridge. An effort is underway by heritage advocates, volunteers and the city government to formally establish a San Pablo Heritage Zone. For a full list of designated heritage sites in the city, see .

chunks.name: San Pedro (Laguna)
chunks.text:
For other cities by the name, see San Pedro (disambiguation).
San Pedro is a city just south of Metro Manila. The city is largely a bedroom community, serving as an important terminus for city buses toward Metro Manila, but there are also local industries. The city's tourist draws include the Sampaguita Festival, the Santo Sepulcro Parish, and the challenging KC Filipinas Golf Club.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
The city forms the major urban sprawl along the South Luzon Expressway. It is the most densely populated city in the CALABARZON region. . It is in Laguna province.

The city was founded as the town of San Pedro de Tunasan by the Spaniards in 1725 from friar lands. Agriculture, duck raising, fishing, and sampaguita production served as the town's source of income, until they all declined in favor of urban development. The city gained its current name in 1902. A significant portion of the hacienda in the town were given to poor farmers under president Ramon Magsaysay's administration, and since became resettlement sites under the National Resettlement and Rehabilitation Administration (NARRA). The city gained city status after a plebiscite in December 2013. Since then, there have been calls for San Pedro to join Metro Manila, but present plans for a merger remain uncertain.

The city gets its name from its patron saint, St. Peter the Apostle (San Pedro Apostol), which also lends its name to the major parish at its Poblacion (town center).

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text:
San Pedro is served by multiple regular city bus routes from Metro Manila, most terminating at bus terminals at Pacita Complex near the boundary with Biñan.

Route 12 Ayala-Biñan from One Ayala in Makati, with most buses terminating at Pacita Complex
Route 15 BGC-Pacita Complex from Market Market in Taguig
Route 38 Fairview-Pacita Complex via Ayala from One Ayala in Makati
Route 39 Fairview-Pacita Complex via C-5, BGC from Market Market in Taguig
Route 46 Navotas-Pacita Complex via Ayala from LRT Buendia station in Pasay and One Ayala in Makati
Route 48 Pacita Complex-Plaza Lawton via Ayala from Plaza Lawton in Manila, LRT Buendia station in Pasay and One Ayala in Makati
Route 53 Cubao-Pacita Complex from Plaza Lawton in Manila and LRT Buendia station in Pasay

Premium bus service is available on UBE Express traveling between Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) and Robinsons Galleria South.

chunks.name: Get in / By car
chunks.text: If you came from NAIA, you can use the South Luzon Expressway. San Pedro is only served by a single exit that only serves as entry and exit southbound. Other alternatives are taking Alabang or Susana Heights/MCX Exit in Muntinlupa (if from Manila) or Southwoods Exit in Biñan (if from elsewhere to the south). National Highway (N1) parallels the South Luzon Expressway, but is always packed by local traffic and jeepneys. It is ill-advised to bring a car in most parts of San Pedro unless you have a GPS map.

chunks.name: Get in / By jeepney
chunks.text: Jeepneys serve San Pedro very well, and there are numerous routes through the city. Most routes through San Pedro originate from Alabang, Biñan, Santa Rosa amd Calamba; some take the expressway and others take the older National Hwy.

chunks.name: Get in / By taxi
chunks.text: Taxis (both car and motorcycle) from Metro Manila also serve San Pedro, especially if you come from the airport, but beware of common scams. Grab and Go Lag taxi service operates in San Pedro.

chunks.name: Get in / By train
chunks.text: There is no train service to San Pedro as of 2026.

chunks.name: Get in / By van
chunks.text: UV Express vans also serve San Pedro; possible drop-off points are in Southwoods (in Biñan) or Pacita Complex. Most of these vans come from Makati or Lipa. Other UV Expres routes serves San Pedro from Festival Alabang, SM Southmall, Nuvali, Molino Bacoor, Cavite, and Pala-Pala (in Dasmariñas).

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: The major forms of public transportation are the tricycle and the jeepney.

It would be better if you stay at hotels in neighboring cities, like in Alabang, Muntinlupa City, to ensure security, quality service and enjoy complete amenities.

chunks.name: San Remigio (Cebu)
chunks.text: San Remigio is a municipality in Cebu Province, on the northwest side of Cebu Island. It has the longest coastline on the island and is an entry point to Bantayan Island via its Hagnaya Port.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: San Remigio has the longest coastline on Cebu Island. As a result, the town is relatively sprawled out along the coast. The town center (Poblacion) is the main commercial center while the barangay of Tambongon hosts a secondary business district for the southern part of the municipality.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text: Intercity buses arrive from and depart to North Bus Terminal in Mandaue, Metro Cebu, about 100 km away. The trip takes 3 to 4 hours depending on traffic. There are three bus terminals in San Remigio. The municipal hall stop serves the town center, while a terminus station located in the barangay of Busogon serves the southern part of the municipality and the Hagnaya Port terminus serves the barangay of Hagnaya and Bantayan Island. Fares start at ₱110.

chunks.name: Get in / By car
chunks.text: San Remigio is easily accessible from Metro Cebu by road via the Central National Highway/Cebu North Hagnaya Wharf Road (signed as Highway 810) which leads directly into the town center and northwards to Hagnaya Port.

chunks.name: Get in / By jeepney
chunks.text: Jeepneys connect San Remigio with Bogo and Tabuelan.

chunks.name: Get in / By boat

chunks.name: San Teodoro (Mindoro)
chunks.text: San Teodoro is a municipality in Oriental Mindoro. It's a quiet place, out of the way of the bustling night-life and commerce of Puerto Galera and Sabang.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
Several ferry lines go to Puerto Galera and Calapan from Batangas. Prices are ₱150-200 per person. It might be worth while to check how long the ride will take, and also the size of the boat, especially if the weather is less than perfect.

There are also Ro-Ro ferries, if you want to bring a car. Depending on size, ₱1000-1200.

When in Mindoro, jeepney's go regularly between Calapan and Puerto Galera. As always in rural Philippines, jeepneys will be packed to the limit, including people on the roof. For a more comfortable ride, rent a van (₱2000-2500 for the day, including driver) or arrange a pick up from your hotel.

The trip from either Puerto Galera or Calapan is around 30 min by car and 1 hour by jeepney (they stop, frequently).

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: By jeepney (Puerto Galera - Calapan) or car/van (rent or arrange via your hotel)

chunks.name: Tamaraw Falls
chunks.text:
A scenic multi-tiered waterfall cascading into natural pools. The lower pool, located under a bridge, offers a refreshing swim in cool mountain water. A few meters upstream, visitors can enjoy stronger waterfalls surrounded by lush greenery. Nearby, a small beach area can be found along the road.
price: Entrance fee applies

chunks.name: Tukuran Falls
chunks.text: A picturesque waterfall surrounded by lush greenery, often reached by a short trek or a carabao (buffalo) ride. The natural pools at the base provide a refreshing swimming spot.

chunks.name: See
chunks.text:
The road going to Puerto Galera is breathtaking, and passes by Tamaraw Falls.
In San Teodoro there are several waterfalls and scenic spots, including Tukuban Falls, Binaybay Falls, Lambingan Falls, Botolan Falls, Aras Falls and caves, Punta (Ilag Point) and Tabunan Hot Springs.

There is a small fish market in the center of town.

chunks.name: Do
chunks.text:
One of San Teodoro's charms is that there's "really nothing to do".
But if it gets too quiet you can swim in one of the above-mentioned falls. In Tamaraw Falls there's man-made pools on the mountain side (entrance ₱25/person), in Tukuban there's natural pools in the forest. The last stretch going to Tukuban includes a hike or carabao ride (₱350 for up to six people) across several streams.

River Kayaking can be arranged, ask your hotel.

Dive or snorkel. The snorkeling is not as good as in Puerto Galera, so you might want to rent a boat (banka).

chunks.name: San Vicente
chunks.text: San Vicente is a small (34,000 in 2020) town in Palawan. It has a very fine beach 14 km (almost nine miles) long and, as of early 2015, is undergoing fairly extensive infrastructure development. Once the airport and some resorts open, it may become a major tourist destination.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: San Vicente is predominantly fishing and a farming municipality and is gaining recognition as a center of interest for tourism. San Vicente can offer a diverse range of attractions for adventure and nature enthusiasts.

chunks.name: Understand / Climate
chunks.text: As with the general climate of the Philippine Archipelago, San Vicente's dry season begins in December, lasting until the month of May while the onset of the wet or rainy season is in June, usually drying up again in November. Northestern winds, the amihan prevail from November to May. Rough coastal waters characterize the season of habagat, or the south-western winds.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text: It is 186 km (116 mi) from Puerto Princesa City.

chunks.name: San Vicente Airport
chunks.text: Flights from Clark International Airport and Manila.

chunks.name: Do
chunks.text: San Vicente's beachfront, popularly called the Long Beach, is being converted into an emerging tourist destination that will be the beneficiary of government spending on infrastructure. The Long Beach have two rocky cliffs interrupting the continuous expanse of approximately 14.7 kilometers of sugary white sand beach dividing it into three coves. It is the longest white sand beach in the Philippines.

chunks.name: Santa
chunks.text: Santa is a town in Ilocos Sur.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
Santa is one of the oldest settlements in Ilocos Sur, having been founded by the Spanish in 1576. It was originally called Santa Catalina de Baba, but was shortened to Santa to avoid confusion with the town of Santa Catalina, west of Vigan. Downtown Santa was built based on a unique octagonal spiderweb layout, with a circular plaza at its center containing the Municipal Hall and the parish church in one side.

The town is hemmed in between the South China Sea to the west and Northern Luzon Heroes Hill National Park, a protected area created from a spur of the Cordillera Mountains isolated from the rest of a range by the Abra River, which forces its way into the South China Sea through a picturesque gorge that marks Santa's boundary with the town of Bantay.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text: Santa is along Route 2 (Manila North Road). Buses heading to Vigan and Laoag also ply this highway.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: Tricycles are the main form of transportation in town.

chunks.name: Northern Luzon Heroes Hill National Park
chunks.text: A 1316 ha ridge that is popular among hikers and motorists for the dramatic coastal views along Manila North Road. Along the highway is a historical marker of heroine Gabriela Silang.

At both ends of the bridge are viewing platforms with panoramic vistas of the area, including the old arch bridge east of the river, which has now lost much of its span following typhoons and flooding.

chunks.name: Santa Ana (Philippines)
chunks.text:
For other places by the name, see Santa Ana.
Santa Ana is a municipality in Cagayan on Luzon, the Philippines. The main beach destination in Cagayan Valley, it also hosts a freeport and is the setting of several overseas survival television series.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
Formerly known as Palauig, Santa Ana is strategically located in a peninsula at the northeasternmost point of Luzon that is also the terminus of the Sierra Madre mountain range. Most settlements are sandwiched between the mountain and the coast, with the town center being on the shores of the Babuyan Channel. The town's Pacific coast is sparsely populated in part due to the rough seas and rugged terrain, and until the 21st century had no road connections with the rest of the country.

During the Spanish era, a lighthouse was built in the island of Palaui to guide galleons traveling to and from Mexico, while succeeding colonizers and the Philippine government built military installations.

In 1995, the area was declared a freeport zone similar to the ones in Olongapo and Clark, allowing for the establishment of a service sector and controversially, casino gambling, which continues to coexist with the town's traditional fishing and nature-based tourism sectors. In the 2000s, Palaui Island became famous for being the setting of two seasons of the American survival reality TV series Survivor. Despite this, Santa Ana has so far managed to avoid the overtourism that has plagued other Philippine resort havens like Boracay. Its beaches are of varying quality. Those along the Babuyan Channel are dark colored, while the white sand beaches are found along the Pacific coast and in Palaui Island.

chunks.name: Understand / Climate
chunks.text: Santa Ana has a tropical monsoon climate with hot, humid conditions prevailing year round. It has an average high temperature of and an average low temperature of .
