chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
Santa Ana is at the northeastern tip of Luzon Island. It is the terminus of the Dugo-San Vicente Road that originates in Camalaniugan, 72 km away, although most travelers enter through Magapit Junction in Lal-lo and follow Magapit-Mision Road, a shortcut that merges with Dugo-San Vicente Road at the boundary of Santa Teresita and Gonzaga towns.

GV Florida and EMC operate once a day bus trips to Santa Ana from Manila. There are also passenger vans to Santa Ana originating from Tuguegarao, as well as jeepneys and minibuses from Aparri.

There is an airstrip at the Camilo Osias Naval Station in Barangay San Vicente, but is reserved for use by the Philippine military. The nearest airport is Cagayan North International Airport in Lal-lo, which only serves charter flights. Most commercial aviation serves Tuguegarao City Airport , 245 km away. It serves domestic flights.

Port San Vicente, at the very end of the Dugo-San Vicente Road, also serves the coastal towns of neighboring Isabela province, although the journey can take more than 8 hours of rough sailing. There are also limited trips to Camiguin de Babuyanes Island, around 4-6 hours sailing time.

A mandatory P20 environmental fee is collected from entering non-residents, with exemptions for children below 10 years old, disabled and elderly persons at the checkpoint marking the boundary with Gonzaga town.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text:
In the mainland, tricycles are the main form of transport. To get to Palaui Island and some beaches on the Pacific coast, rent a boat at Port San Vicente. Prices can range from P900 to P4950 depending on your itinerary.

Make sure the boat is fit for passenger transport and do not accept offers to sail on small fishermen's boats, as they are unregistered. In the event of an accident, you may be detained at the Coast Guard Substation at the port.

chunks.name: Cape Engaño Lighthouse
chunks.text:

From the complex, multiple islands can be viewed on a clear day, such as Dos Hermanos Island, Didicas Volcano and Camiguin de Babuyanes Island. All visitors must register at Engaño Cove and be accompanied by an accredited tour guide.
address: Palaui Island

chunks.name: Santa Cruz (Laguna)
chunks.text: For other cities by the name, see Santa Cruz (disambiguation).

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: The town was established from the barrios (or barangays in modern times) of then-larger Lumban by the Spaniards in 1602. It became the capital of Laguna in 1858. The town's history is filled with disasters, from typhoons, floods, and numerous battles. Santa Cruz has been a scene of battles during the Philippine Revolution, the Philippine–American War, and the Pacific War; the town has since recovered and is now the economic and transportation hub of eastern Laguna.

chunks.name: Understand / Orientation
chunks.text: The town center lies near the mouth of the Santa Cruz river and is bisected by it. There are two bridges crossing over the river in the downtown. The Calamba-Pagsanjan Road passes through the southern suburbs and forms a junction leading to downtown in Barangay Pagsawitan, where the bus terminals are located. All jeepney terminals, except those heading for Lucban, which are located in Pagsawitan Junction and Metro Central Mall, are scattered in the town center. To alleviate traffic entering the downtown from Calamba, vehicles turn left at the junction in Barangay Bubukal, which is a secondary commercial hub, towards Quezon Avenue heading to the Santa Cruz Bridge.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text: From Manila, the main route to Santa Cruz is from the Calamba-Pagsanjan Road, exiting from Turbina exit of the South Luzon Expressway (SLEX) in Calamba. From the east, Manila East Road loops around Rizal and the lakeside towns of eastern Laguna before joining Calamba-Pagsanjan Road in Pagsanjan, where a right turn leads to Santa Cruz. From Nagcarlan, a two-lane road runs north to Bubukal Junction in Santa Cruz.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text:
Santa Cruz is well served by buses from the major provincial bus terminals in Metro Manila; travel times take about 2 hours (or more with traffic jams), including a major stop in Calamba.

DLTB provides frequent half-hourly departures from the company's Buendia (Pasay) and Cubao (Quezon City) terminals.
JAC Liner (formerly Greenstar Express) provides 30-minute departures from their terminal at Taft/Buendia in Pasay.
HM Liner and Worthy Transport has hourly departures to their terminal in Barangay Pagsawitan, Pagsanjan, beside the boundary with Santa Cruz; buses leave from Cubao or Alabang (South Station). Alabang-bound buses include two stopovers in Calamba: Mayapa and SM Calamba/Crossing.

Average fares are ₱40 from Calamba, ₱140 from Alabang, ₱170 from ﹰBuendia, and ₱190 from Pasay.

chunks.name: Santa Fe (Nueva Vizcaya)
chunks.text:
For other places by the name, see Santa Fe.
Santa Fe is a town in Nueva Vizcaya, Philippines. Situated at the base of two mountain passes, it is the main point of entry leading to the Cagayan Valley region from Metro Manila by road.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
For much of its history, Santa Fe, formerly known as Imugan, was a small village along the headwaters of the Magat River at the foot of the Caraballo mountains separating the Cagayan Valley from the Central Luzon plains. It gained prominence for its strategic location at the terminus of the Balete (Dalton) and Malico Passes, which led to its inclusion into the Philippine highway network and a bloody battle in the closing days of World War II in 1945 that saw American and Filipino forces engage in months of protracted uphill fighting against Japanese holdouts in the said passes as part of the Liberation of Cagayan Valley.

Tucked into the meeting point of the Caraballo and Cordillera mountain ranges and the quadruple boundary between Nueva Vizcaya, Nueva Ecija, Pangasinan and Benguet provinces, Santa Fe is an ethnically mixed town inhabited by Ilocano migrants, Igorot tribespeople and indigenous Kalanguya. While not exactly a tourist town, its main attractions are from a natural and logistical perspective, being a midway point in the journey between Metro Manila and Cagayan Valley with loads of roadside restaurants and gas stations serving tired motorists who are also pondering the mountain views.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
Santa Fe lies along the Maharlika Highway, formally known as the Pan-Philippine or Asian Highway (AH 26). The main entrance to the town and the rest of Cagayan Valley, it is a two-lane thoroughfare that is vulnerable to traffic jams caused by landslides, vehicular accidents and vehicles sustaining mechanical breakdowns, particularly in the mountainous section leading from Balete (Dalton) Pass at the boundary with Carranglan in Nueva Ecija.

The Pangasinan-Nueva Vizcaya Road (Malico Road), an alternate route to decongest the Maharlika Highway, connects Santa Fe with San Nicolas in Pangasinan via Salacsac Pass, but its usage is limited only to light vehicles and is more dangerous to navigate for the less experienced motorist with its winding switchbacks and lack of guardrails. Unlike Dalton Pass, Malico is sometimes closed when typhoons approach.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text: Santa Fe is a midway point and major stopover for buses travelling between Metro Manila and Cagayan Valley.

chunks.name: Get in / By jeep
chunks.text: The intermunicipal jeepney service that runs through the main towns of Nueva Vizcaya has its southern terminus at Santa Fe.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: Tricycles are the most common transport between barangays, but due to uneven terrain, an SUV or any 4WD is recommended, particularly when driving along Dalton Pass or Malico Road.

chunks.name: Dalton Pass
chunks.text:
It is a rugged piece of terrain where a part of the Caraballo Sur reaches south and joins the Sierra Madre. Because of its strategic importance as the only access between Nueva Ecija and Cagayan Valley, the pass became the scene of much bloody fighting during the final stages of World War II. Japanese Shobu soldiers headed by General Tomoyuki Yamashita tried to hold their positions while Filipino and American soldiers under the leadership of Colonel Robert Lapham, were determined to dislodge them from February to March 1945. By the close of hostilities, the blood of almost seventeen thousand Japanese fighting units and the US-Filipino allied forces mingled with the soil. Markers that commemorate their sacrifice stand by the road’s highest point, with good view into the highlands. The shrine is a reminder for Gen. James L. Dalton who was killed by a sniper’s bullet during the end of World War II. At above sea level, Dalton Pass is the gateway to Cagayan Valley.
address: Maharlika Highway, Tactac

chunks.name: Salacsac Pass
chunks.text:
The site of a World-War II battle fought in conjunction with the Battle of Dalton Pass. Unlike Dalton, the site sits on a higher altitude and is a newly-developed site that was opened following the concreting of the Pangasinan-Nueva Vizcaya Road in the early 2020s. There are stalls selling coffee and agricultural goods and a war memorial. On a clear day, the mines of Itogon in Benguet province can be seen to the west, as well as the Central Luzon plains as far south as Nueva Ecija and Tarlac. However, the area is claimed by both the provinces of Nueva Vizcaya and Pangasinan, which views the area as part of the municipality of San Nicolas.
address: Pangasinan-Nueva Vizcaya Rd, Barangay Malico

chunks.name: Imugan Falls

Also within the area is the Imugan Mountain Fresh Factory which utilizes wild berries and other fruits to produce spreads and jams while visitors can watch the production process and shop for preserved fruit spreads.

chunks.name: Santa Maria (Bulacan)
chunks.text:
For other cities by the name, see Santa Maria.
Santa Maria is a municipality in the province of Bulacan, Philippines. It is a growing commercial hub in the Bulacan plains that is gradually becoming a commuter town of Metro Manila.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
Previously a barrio of Bocaue, Santa Maria was established as an independent town during the Spanish era in 1793. Founded as Santa Maria de Pandi after the large hacienda estate of which it was part of, it was shortened to Santa Maria to avoid confusion with the neighboring settlement of Pandi, which used to be part of Bigaa (Balagtas) and became a separate town in 1946.

Despite being bypassed by the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) in the 1970s, its proximity to the Bocaue Exit, 3 km away, has led to an influx of commuter workers serving Metro Manila, industrial warehouses and other commercial enterprises.

As of 2024, Santa Maria has a population of 322,525 people.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
From Metro Manila, take NLEX Bocaue Exit and turn right along Governor Fortunato Halili Avenue leading to Santa Maria. An alternate route is through NLEX Ciudad de Victoria Exit leading to bypass roads connecting it with Halili Avenue, though this may be closed if there are major events in the nearby Philippine Arena.

From Trinoma and SM North EDSA in Quezon City, a point-to-point bus leaves every 30 minutes from 6:30AM to 10:30PM for Caypombo, a northern barangay of Santa Maria, with a stopover at WalterMart Santa Maria in Barangay Santa Clara, where tricycles can be taken to downtown Santa Maria for up to P60. A one-way bus fare to WalterMart costs P100, while fares to Caypombo reach P120. Santa Maria is also served by commuter buses heading from Metro Manila to the neighboring towns of Angat and Norzagaray.

There are also jeepneys connecting Santa Maria with Monumento in Caloocan, Metro Manila, as well as other Bulacan destinations such as Pandi, Baliwag, Bocaue, Malolos, Meycauayan, San Jose del Monte, Angat and Norzagaray. The main jeepney terminal is below Santa Maria Bridge and occupies a promenade along the Santa Maria River.

To avoid traffic in downtown Santa Maria, a bypass road skirts the west of town from Puregold Halili Avenue, passing through WalterMart before joining Norzagaray-Santa Maria Road further north.

chunks.name: Santa Rita
chunks.text: Santa Rita is a town in southwestern Pampanga, Philippines. It is a quiet agricultural town bypassed by the province's major highways.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: Santa Rita was established in 1697, having been separated from Porac. Bypassed by major highways and notwithstanding damage caused by the Mount Pinatubo eruption in 1991, it has managed to retain a significant number of its colonial era houses.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
Santa Rita is bypassed by the major highways of Pampanga. From Manila, take the San Fernando exit along the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) leading to the Gapan-Olongapo Road, also known as Jose Abad Santos Avenue (JASA). From San Fernando, go west towards Guagua, then turn right at the junction with signage pointing to Santa Rita. A parallel road, Dalan Betis, also connects the town with Betis district of Guagua.

From San Fernando and Guagua, there are jeepneys servicing downtown Santa Rita and its subsidiary barangay of Dila-dila, on the boundary with Porac. Fares from Guagua cost P13. The town is also a stopover along the Porac-Guagua jeepney route. From Metro Manila, take a bus going to Zambales or Bataan and disembark along JASA at the junction in Guagua heading to Santa Rita.

chunks.name: Santa Rosa (Laguna)
chunks.text:
For other places by the name, see Santa Rosa.
Santa Rosa is a city in Laguna, a light industrial and commercial hub close to Metro Manila. Major tourist draws are the Enchanted Kingdom theme park, the Nuvali mixed-use development, and shopping spots like SM City Santa Rosa and Paseo de Santa Rosa. Santa Rosa is a major stopover for travelers to Tagaytay via Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road (Route 420).

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
Santa Rosa is one of the largest cities in Laguna, forming the urban sprawl along the western coast of Laguna de Bay. The city is one of the most densely-populated cities of Laguna, ahead of San Pedro. Despite the industrial and commercial developments in the city, Santa Rosa still serves as a bedroom community south of Manila.

It is best known as a regional industrial center, home to major producers like Toyota Motors Philippines, Monde Nissin and Coca-Cola Philippines, lending its nickname "Lion City of the Philippines". There are also industrial parks and major residential communities.

The city was founded from parts of the pueblo of Tabuko (present-day Cabuyao), and first named Bukol (Bucol). It was renamed as Santa Rosa, after Saint Rose of Lima, in 1792. Agriculture and family businesses once served a major component in the local economy until urbanization began in the 1970s, which gave the city's present appearance.

. The local population is mostly Tagalog, but there are also expat communities formed by Chinese and Americans. Significant local migrant populations of Visayans also exist. Most Western expats live in affluent communities, generally gated subdivisions.

chunks.name: Understand / Orientation
chunks.text:
Santa Rosa's growth is horizontal, just like the other sprawling cities nearby, and the South Luzon Expressway (SLEx) can serve as an important boundary between the industrialized and commercialized west and residential east. The sides of the city shows contrasts: eastern Santa Rosa is the crowded, noisy and ordinarily Filipino old city, while western Santa Rosa is mostly industrial and affluent in character (exceptions are barangays Pulong Santa Cruz and Santo Domingo, which are crowded barangays).

The Balibago area is home to cheap shopping and the major transport terminal. The Poblacion, rather a lumping of five barangays, contains the old downtown and government offices. National Highway (Route 1) is the main commercial street, home to large malls like SM City Santa Rosa and Robinsons Santa Rosa Market. Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road (Route 420) hosts most of the city's industries, and the section between Paseo de Santa Rosa and Nuvali houses classy shopping and dining.

chunks.name: Understand / Tourist information
chunks.text: Information for tourists about sights and places to eat can be found at the Visit Santa Rosa page of the city government.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text:
Some bus companies from Metro Manila have terminals in Balibago, along the junction with the Manila South Road and the Santa Rosa-Tagaytay. Another city bus connection is by way of Biñan. Take the route 15 Ayala-Biñan bus, and transfer to the Biñan-Balibago jeepney.

From the south, some bus routes terminate at the , beside SM City Santa Rosa, but as of 2025, the terminal remains deserted and bus companies that used to serve it terminating at Manila terminals instead.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text:
UBE Express operates point-to-point buses from Ninoy Aquino International Airport and get down at either Seda Nuvali or Robinson's Santa Rosa Market. Fares cost at about ₱190.
TAS Transport operates point-to-point buses to Nuvali from Circuit Makati, for ₱150 one-way. Buses depart every 20 minutes from 7-8 AM, half-hourly from 8-9 AM, hourly from 9AM-5PM, and 20 minutes from 5-8PM

chunks.name: Get in / By jeepney
chunks.text:
From Alabang in Muntinlupa, you can take an express jeepney from South Station into Balibago terminal. The whole trip costs ₱38, but taking a provincial bus is far cheaper (but you need to wait at the bus stop under the Alabang Viaduct). On the terminal in Balibago, transfers to local jeepneys or tricycles are available.

Santa Rosa also lies on the busy jeepney route between San Pedro and Calamba.

chunks.name: Get in / By car
chunks.text:
If you drive, you can take the South Luzon Expressway (SLEX), which has 2 exits serving the city:
Santa Rosa Exit (exit 38) - Enchanted Kingdom, Balibago Complex, Paseo de Santa Rosa and Nuvali. This can get packed during weekends and holidays when many travelers head to Enchanted Kingdom, Nuvali, and Tagaytay.
ETON City Exit - Alternative exit if going to Paseo de Santa Rosa or Nuvali

You can take Mamplasan Exit (exit 36) in nearby Biñan if you are going to SM City Santa Rosa. Once you exit in Mamplasan, drive Greenfield Avenue for a distance, then turn to Santa Rosa Access Road. Note that the access road is closed at some times.

chunks.name: Get in / By train
chunks.text: There is no train service to Santa Rosa as of 2026. Construction is ongoing for an electrified railway line going from Manila to Calamba.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text:
You can bring your car with you to visit most attractions in the city, but beware: traffic jams and driving behaviors are not for the faint-hearted. Most tourist spots like Enchanted Kingdom, Paseo de Santa Rosa and Nuvali can be easily reached by car, but alternatives are available.

You can also take a jeepney once you get down the bus or express jeepney in Balibago, and it will bring you to most locations in the city. Fares start at ₱8 for the first and an additional ₱2 for each additional kilometer.

The Poblacion area is best accessed through tricycles and foot, but the roads are narrow and watch out for vehicles if you walk.

chunks.name: Enchanted Kingdom
chunks.text:
Opened in 1995, this fantasy-themed amusement park is the city's number one tourist draw, drawing locals and foreigners (generally Chinese and Koreans) alike. The park is built with Filipino values in mind, and not just for amusement and thrill-seeking. Go ride the Wheel of Fate and see the wide views of the city and surrounding area, spin around in the Space Shuttle roller coaster, get wet at the Jungle Log Jam, drive a go-kart on their tracks, or take pictures with the park's mascots Eldar and Princess Victoria.
hours: Mon Tue closed, Wed Thu 11AM-7PM, Fri noon-7PM, Sat 11AM-9PM, Sun 10AM-9PM; address: San Lorenzo Road, San Jose

chunks.name: Santa Rosa Arch
chunks.text:
19th-century welcome arch based on Paris's Arc de Triomphe, with the current arch being Art Deco, built in the 1930s. It is a local symbol, found in the city's official seal.
address: J.P. Rizal Avenue, Malusak

chunks.name: Santa Rosa de Lima Parish Church
chunks.text:
The main Roman Catholic church in the city, built in 1796.
address: F. Gomez Street, Kanluran

chunks.name: Balibago Complex
chunks.text:
The traditional commercial heart of the city, which also hosts the bus terminals.
address: National Highway, Balibago

chunks.name: Paseo Outlets
chunks.text:
Lifestyle mall, part of the Greenfield City private township which spreads into neighboring Cabuyao. Shops and restaurants are spread out in 9 buildings, with their own parking lots.
hours: 10AM-11PM

chunks.name: SM City Santa Rosa
chunks.text:
A huge two-storey mall with a vast collection of shops and restaurants, cinemas, a department store, and supermarket. Since 2017, it hosts tower blocks housing call centers. Also at the mall grounds is the SRIT (see #Get in).
hours: 10AM-9PM; address: National Highway, Tagapo

chunks.name: Robinsons Santa Rosa
chunks.text:
Three-storey mall, with fewer shops and restaurants. Has a supermarket and cinema, but no department store. Used to be frequented by locals before the opening of its rival, SM City Santa Rosa.
hours: 10AM–8PM; address: National Highway, Tagapo

chunks.text:
A members-only warehouse grocery.
hours: 9AM-9PM; address: Lot 1, Block 13, Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road, Nuvali, Santo Domingo

chunks.name: Landers Superstore Nuvali
chunks.text:
A members-only warehouse grocery.
hours: 9AM–9PM; address: Nuvali Boulevard corner Evoliving Center Drive, Don Jose

chunks.text: hours: 9AM–9PM; address: Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road corner San Lorenzo, Balibago

chunks.name: WalterMart Santa Rosa Bel-Air
chunks.text: hours: 9AM-8PM; address: Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road, Pulong Santa Cruz

chunks.name: Robinsons Easymart Dita

chunks.text: hours: 8AM-9PM; address: Golden City Subdivision, Dila

chunks.name: El Cielito Inn
chunks.text:
The El Cielito Inn, a member of the respected family of Philippine low-cost, high-quality inns, is conveniently located near the Convention Center and SM City.
price: From ₱2000; address: Sta. Rosa-Tagaytay Road, Pulong Santa Cruz

chunks.name: Seda Nuvali
chunks.text:
Part of chain of luxury hotels owned by Ayala. Rooms have cable TV, iPad docks, a small bar, and tea and coffee makers. Amenities include outdoor pool, laundry, free breakfast, kids playroom and restaurant. The rooms provide a view of Nuvali and surrounding area. There is a bus connection from Ninoy Aquino International Airport, and also free parking if you drive. Its location is not too far from the other tourist draws of Nuvali, which stretches into Cabuyao and Calamba.
price: From ₱3765; address: Evozone Avenue, Nuvali, Don Jose

chunks.name: Hotel Sogo Santa Rosa
chunks.text:
Part of motel chain with distinctive red and yellow buildings. A/C rooms with cable TV, bathroom and WiFi. Parking is available, and you can also order meals inside.
price: ₱1150; address: Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road, Pulong Santa Cruz

chunks.name: Santander (Cebu)
chunks.text: Santander is the southernmost municipality in Cebu Province, 137 km from Cebu City. It does not attract many tourists on its own merits, though there are some beach resorts. It does get quite a few travellers passing through, mostly because it has a ferry terminal that is on the main bus route between Dumaguete and Metro Cebu.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
Santander is on the coastal highway that runs around Cebu Island and is therefore reachable by road from almost anywhere on the island. Common starting points for journeys to Santander are the nearby resort area of Moalboal or the South Bus Terminal in Cebu City.

There are ferries to/from Sibulan in Negros Oriental and to/from Siquijor. The Cebu-Dumaguete bus route crosses to Sibulan here, then goes on to nearby Dumaguete.

The ferry terminal is in barangay Bato, a bit west of the town along the highway.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: For local transport, tricycles are abundant. Travellers bound for Moalboal usually use one to get from the ferry terminal to the bus station.

chunks.name: Eat
chunks.text: The ferry terminals have restaurants serving plain but filling Filipino food at moderate prices.

chunks.name: Santiago (Ilocos Sur)
chunks.text:
For other cities by the name, see Santiago (disambiguation).
Santiago is a town in Ilocos Sur with extensive beaches and a Spanish-era watchtower.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: Santiago was established by the Spanish sometime during the 18th century. It was named after Saint James the Apostle after he was credited with handing a military victory to the Spanish against a marauding Moro pirate fleet in what is now Santiago Cove.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text: Santiago is along Route 2 (Manila North Road). Buses heading to Vigan and Laoag also ply this highway. Near the southern boundary with Candon is a junction leading to Banayoyo and other upland towns of Ilocos Sur and Mountain Province.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: Tricycles are the main form of transportation in town, particularly as downtown Santiago is further inland from the coast.

chunks.name: Ambucao Beach
chunks.text:
An extensive stretch of cream-colored sand running to Biak na Bato aka Mapisi Rock, a rock formation marking the boundary with the town of San Esteban.
address: Ambucao

chunks.name: Santiago Cove
chunks.text:
The town's main draw, a horseshoe-shaped bay surrounded by Sabangan Beach, stretch of white-sand beach dubbed the “Boracay of the North”.
address: Sabangan

chunks.name: St. James the Greater Parish Church
chunks.text:
Santiago's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style by the Spanish during the late 18th century on a hilltop. It also functioned as a fortress against pirates and foreign invaders at the time.
address: Manila North Road, Poblacion Norte

chunks.name: Mapisi Rock
chunks.text:
A rocky promontory with a walkway and viewdeck at the top.
address: Ambucao

chunks.name: Sabangan Watchtower
chunks.text:
A stout, Spanish-era watchtower overlooking Santiago Cove meant to guard against pirates and foreign invaders from the South China Sea. The site was declared a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 2015.
address: Sabangan Road, Sabangan

chunks.name: Vitalis Villas
chunks.text:
A luxury accommodation overlooking Santiago Cove and architecturally inspired by the houses of Santorini in Greece.
address: Sabangan Road, Sabangan

chunks.name: Santiago Cove Hotel and Restaurant
chunks.text:
A resort overlooking Santiago Cove
address: Sabangan Road, Sabangan

chunks.name: Corals, Sand and Shells Beach House
chunks.text: address: Zone 4, San Roque

chunks.name: Vitalis White Sands
chunks.text: address: Sabangan Road, Sabangan

chunks.name: Santiago City
chunks.text: For Santiago of Chile, see Santiago. For other cities by the name, see Santiago (disambiguation).

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: Founded by the Spanish during the 18th century, it was originally called Carig, before being renamed after its patron saint. In 1994 it became the first legally-designated city in the Cagayan Valley Region, owing to its strategic location at the spot where the Maharlika Highway from Manila branches out into different routes leading to Quirino Province, Tuguegarao and the Mallig Plains. It also forms a minor metropolitan area that includes the neighboring municipalities of Cordon, San Isidro and Ramon.

chunks.name: Victory Liner Bus Terminal
chunks.text: address: R.C. Miranda Boulevard, Calao West

chunks.name: GV Florida Bus Terminal
chunks.text: address: Maharlika Highway, Calao East

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
Santiago is on the Maharlika Highway (Pan-Philippine Highway, Asian Highway 26), and is a key destination for buses from Metro Manila. It is the hub of public transportation to other towns of southern Isabela and the neighboring provinces of Ifugao, Quirino and Nueva Vizcaya. It is also the terminus of the Tuguegarao-Roxas-Santiago Road, which runs parallel to Maharlika Highway in western Isabela up to Tuguegarao in Cagayan. Long-distance commutes are handled by buses, while commuters to neighboring provinces usually ride passenger vans.

There is frequent bus service along the Cagayan Valley Road, between Manila and Tuguegarao. There are also less frequent buses connecting the city with Baguio, Abra province, and cities in the Ilocos region.

The jeepney fare from Solano to Santiago is ₱60. The a/c bus fare from Santiago to Tuguegarao is ₱190.

The nearest airport is in Cauayan, an hour’s drive.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: Tricycles are the main public transportation mode within the city. Fares start at P20.

chunks.name: Calvary Hills and The Chapel of Transfiguration
chunks.text:
The place offers a pilgrimage venue for the Holy Week where life-size Stations of the Cross are presented from the foot of the hill going all the way up to the top where a Chapel was so designed to face the rising sun. The Chapel of Transfiguration offers pilgrims a commanding silence befitting a place of worship and can also be utilized for masses and retreat venues. A life-size image of Our Lady of La Salette also stands at the site, facing the City.
hours: Open 24 hours; price: Free; address: Dariok Hills, Balintocatoc

chunks.name: Balay Na Santiago
chunks.text:
This used to be a barangay hall called Palacio del Barrio located at Calao West. Balay na Santiago houses the city museum and city library. This also serves as a multi-purpose function hall for art and music exhibitions and different occasion. The building itself is of the bahay na bato style popular during the Spanish colonial era.
address: Melegrito Street

chunks.name: Santiago Concrete Water Tank
chunks.text:
This concrete water tank has been a landmark in Santiago City since the early 1970s. It is almost 30 meters high, and towers over the whole city, visible from almost anywhere. It was constructed through the help of then Congressman Delfin Albano of the lone district of Isabela, and under the leadership of then Mayor Dodo Miranda. It was turned into a colorful mural and is now considered a City Heritage Treasure.
hours: Open 24 hours; price: Free; address: 3 Carreon Street

chunks.name: Museo de Pattaradday
chunks.text:
This museum at houses collection of artifacts, relics, dresses and antique furniture showing the culture and traditions that are typical in this region of Northeastern Luzon. Temporary closed as of September 2023.
address: Centro East

chunks.name: Magat Dam
chunks.text:
Opened in 1983, it was deemed the largest dam in Southeast Asia at the time and created a reservoir that displaced numerous communities in neighboring Ifugao. Since then it is one of the main sources of irrigation and electricity in the Cagayan Valley Region. The complex and its surroundings have become a favorite recreation spot for residents as well as day-trippers from Santiago. Fishing activities are also available at the reservoir.
address: Burgos-General Aguinaldo Road, Barangay General Aguinaldo, Ramon

Has a nice food court on the 2nd floor.
hours: 10AM–9PM; address: Maharlika Highway, Mabini

chunks.name: Santo Domingo (Ilocos Sur)
chunks.text: Santo Domingo is a coastal town in Ilocos Sur.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: Santo Domingo was founded by the Spanish in 1742.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
Santo Domingo is along Route 2 (Manila North Road). Buses heading to Laoag also ply this highway.

The nearest cruise ship terminal is in Salomague Port in Cabugao, 24 km to the north.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: Tricycles are the main form of transportation in town, particularly as downtown Santo Domingo is further inland from the coast.

chunks.name: Saint Dominic de Guzman Parish Church
chunks.text:
Santo Domingo's main Roman Catholic church, built during the Spanish era in a baroque style in 1740. Diego Silang, who later led the biggest anti-Spanish revolt in the Ilocos Region in 1762, served as a bell ringer at the parish.
address: Nalasin

chunks.name: Unknown Citizen Park
chunks.text:
A small monument dedicated to the anonymous citizens of the municipality.
address: Manila North Road, San Pablo

chunks.name: Rizal Park
chunks.text:
The main recreational and green space in town, featuring a monument to the national hero, Jose Rizal, that was erected in 1972, and Monumento ti Pagulidanan, an obelisk-like contraption built to celebrate unity and notable residents.
address: Manila North Road, Poblacion

chunks.name: Sived Beach
chunks.text:
A 6 km stretch of gray sand in the northwestern side of town ideal for surfing.
address: Sived

chunks.name: Puerto Beach
chunks.text:
A stretch of sand along the southwestern side of town. It has the ruins of a jetty built by the Japanese during World War II.
address: Calay-ab

chunks.name: Santo Domingo Public Market
chunks.text: address: Manila North Road corner A. Bonifacio Street, Vacunero

chunks.name: Santo Domingo (Philippines)
chunks.text: Santo Domingo is a municipality of the Philippines in the east coast of Albay province, flanked by the provincial capital, Legazpi and the municipality of Bacacay accessible via Legazpi-Tiwi coastal road. Resorts along the town's coastline offer a wonderful view of the black beach and is on the Albay Gulf often frequented by whale sharks. It is one of the five municipalities that has a jurisdiction over the foothills of Mayon Volcano.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: The town was once called Libog, but it was renamed Santo Domingo in 1959. It is the birthplace of the famous classic Bicolano song, Sarong Banggi, composed by Potenciano Gregorio.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text: There are buses from Manila to Santo Domingo, stopping also at other towns and cities along the way, and there are also jeepneys from Legazpi at Legazpi Grand Central Terminal right in front of SM City Legazpi.

chunks.name: Get in / By car
chunks.text: Santo Domingo is 12 km from Legazpi and 539 km from Manila.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: Around the town center there are pedicabs while tricycles are available heading to the outlying barangays.

chunks.name: See
chunks.text:
Parish of Saint Dominic of Guzman
Mirisbiris Garden and Nature Center — Purok 3, Brgy. Salvacion
Aguas Farm - barangay Fidel Surtida
Reyes Beach Resort - barangay Calayucay
Captains M Private Resort - barangay San Isidro
Sarung Banggi Boulevard

chunks.name: Do
chunks.text:
There are some ATV rentals.
Sarung Banggi Festival — an eight-day summer festivity immortalizing Potenciano Gregorio, Sr.'s timeless composition is held here annually in the month of May.

chunks.name: Eat
chunks.text: There are eateries in Santo Domingo Public Market.

chunks.name: Tres Hijos Hotel & Resort
chunks.text: price: ₱230 (adult), ₱200 (Senior/PWD), ₱100 (Kids); address: Barangay San Isidro

chunks.name: Costa Palmera Resort
chunks.text: address: Purok 3, Calayucay

chunks.name: Go next
chunks.text:
Legazpi - just adjacent very easy to reach.
Tabaco - a jeepney ride away from Santo Domingo.

chunks.name: Santo Tomas (Batangas)
chunks.text:
For other places by the name, see Santo Tomas.
Santo Tomas is a city in Batangas. It is the main gateway to Batangas from Manila, and is a growing industrial and commercial center.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
Santo Tomas lies just south of Batangas's boundary with Laguna, and is a major road junction, serving the Maharlika Highway (Route 1 and Asian Highway 26) and Jose P. Laurel Highway (Route 4). The town takes its name from its patron saint, St. Thomas Aquinas, also the patron saint of Catholic schools. Santo Tomas is also the hometown of the Filipino general Miguel Malvar, who led the soldiers of the Tagalog Republic during the Philippine–American War, and also the last general to surrender to the Americans.

Santo Tomas forms part of the vast sprawl from Metro Manila which ends at Lipa. It became a city in 2019, after a successful local plebiscite. Santo Tomas's economy is largely based on manufacturing, agriculture and real estate development. Suburbanization has resulted in most agricultural land becoming part of the sprawl.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text: Most provincial buses headed between Manila and Lipa, Batangas City, Quezon Province and Bicol stop at Santo Tomas. Jeepneys between Calamba and San Pablo, Tanauan, and Lipa serve the city proper.

chunks.name: Get in / By car
chunks.text:
From Manila and Calamba, take the South Luzon Expressway (SLEX) and exit at Santo Tomas. Alternatively, take the older and congested Maharlika Highway/National (Route 1).

From Lipa/Batangas City, take the STAR Tollway and exit at Santo Tomas. Alternatively, you can exit at Tanauan or avoid the toll altogether and take the older and congested Jose P. Laurel Highway (Route 4)

From Quezon Province or Bicol, follow the Maharlika Highway (Route 1/AH26)

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: The town is served by jeepneys in major thoroughfares, and tricycles in all other nooks and crannies not served by jeepneys. Car travel is advisable, especially when visiting the Padre Pio Shrine, but prepare for traffic jams in feast days and at the queue for the STAR Tollway exit, particularly during rush hour. In the worst case scenario, such gridlock can extend as far as San Pablo, 17 km away in Laguna province.

chunks.name: General Miguel Malvar Shrine
chunks.text:
Houses a statue and a museum on Miguel Malvar, Filipino general of the Tagalog Republic during the Philippine-American War.
hours: 8AM–4PM; closed Mondays and holidays; price: Free. Donation optional; address: Malvar Street, Barangay 1

chunks.name: Parish and International Shrine of Saint Padre Pio
chunks.text:
A Roman Catholic shrine and parish devoted to St. Padre Pio of Pietrelcina, with buildings built to local styles. Built as a small chapel along Maharlika Highway, it is now a large complex frequented by devotees around Batangas and surrounding provinces, as well as Metro Manila. It was recognized as an international shrine by the Vatican in 2026.
address: Gov. Antonio Carpio Avenue, San Pedro

chunks.name: Saint Thomas Aquinas Parish
chunks.text:
There is little known about the church's early history, but it dates back to around the 17th century, when Santo Tomas town center was established. The old church was destroyed by American artillery bombardment during World War II in 1945, and was replaced by a modernist church building and belfry. There is a memorial to the 15 Holy Spirit Sisters, mostly Germans, who died.
address: General Malvar Street

chunks.name: Mount Makiling
chunks.text: A towering inactive volcano and prime hiking destination shared with the town of Los Baños in Laguna.

chunks.name: SM City Santo Tomas
chunks.text: hours: 10AM–9PM; address: 20 Maharlika Highway, Barangay San Roque

chunks.name: Santo Tomas City Market
chunks.text: address: Maharlika Highway, Barangay II

chunks.name: S&R Membership Shopping Santo Tomas
chunks.text:
A members-only warehouse grocery.
hours: 9AM-9PM; address: Maharlika Highway, San Roque

chunks.name: The Lifestyle Strip
chunks.text:
Strip mall with various restaurants and coffee shop.
address: Maharlika Highway, San Antonio

chunks.name: Rose & Grace
chunks.text:
A restaurant serving bulalo (beef bone soup) since 1970.
hours: 6AM-10PM; address: Malvar Street corner Maharlika Highway

chunks.name: Microtel Inn & Suites
chunks.text:
A/C rooms equipped with cable TV and radio clock. The inn has a swimming pool, meeting room and Wifi connection.
address: First Philippine Industrial Park

chunks.name: Santol
chunks.text: Santol is a town in La Union.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: Named after the local term for Sandoricum koetjape, a fruit-bearing tree, Santol is a landlocked municipality established at the foothills of the Luzon Cordilleras. Its area extends through down to the Amburayan River bordering the highland town of Sugpon in Ilocos Sur and Benguet, and is home to significant Igorot communities. Formerly a part of the Amburayan subdistrict of Mountain Province, it was annexed by La Union in 1920.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text: Santol is bypassed by Manila North Road (Route 2), the main thoroughfare in La Union. Instead, it is connected to the highway by a road leading to the neighboring coastal municipality of Balaoan.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: Tricycles are the main form of transportation in town. However, some of the mountain areas can only be reached by either 4WD or hired motorcycle.

chunks.name: Balay Anito Falls
chunks.text:
Meaning "House of the Spirits", it is a cascade that drops down to a 20 m deep pool.
address: Sitio Banbanaba, Lettac Sur

chunks.name: Puy-ocan Falls
chunks.text:
A secluded cascade whose crashing waters produce a mist-like effect.
address: Sapdaan

chunks.name: Simminublan Falls
chunks.text:
A cascade whose name derives from the cooking pot-like shape of its basin.
address: Sitio Bilagan, Puquil

chunks.name: Lengsad Falls
chunks.text:
A cascade leading down to the Amburayan River.
address: Sitio Inasan, Tubaday

chunks.name: Sasaba Rice Terraces
chunks.text:
A terraced farming complex on the slopes of the Cordillera Mountains.
address: Sasaba

chunks.name: Meditation Cross
chunks.text:
A large concrete cross overlooking downtown Santol that is commonly visited during Holy Week.
address: Poblacion

chunks.name: Santol Green Market
chunks.text:
The town's main marketplace.
address: Poblacion

chunks.name: Sleep
chunks.text: The nearest accommodations are in Balaoan.

chunks.name: Sariaya
chunks.text: Sariaya is a town in western Quezon. Along with neighboring Tayabas, it houses many Spanish-era cultural monuments and is nicknamed the "Heritage Capital of Quezon". Its seaside is filled with resorts, continuing from those in San Juan in Batangas.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
Sariaya is from Manila and from the provincial capital, Lucena. It is surrounded by Mount Banahaw to the north, Tayabas Bay to the south, the town of Candelaria to the west, and Tayabas to the east. Part of the municipality lies along the coast, and has the resorts.

Like its neighbor, Tayabas, Sariaya town center is known for its Spanish and American-era architecture, notably its Art Deco mansions. The municipality is striving to have the town center declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and is working to restore its historical buildings.

The municipality has a growing number of beach resorts, concentrated at the seaside community of Guisguis, and the construction of the Quezon Eco-Tourism Road has helped improved access to the once-secluded beaches.

chunks.name: Supreme
chunks.text:
Frequent service between Batangas City and Lucena via Rosario, San Juan, and Candelaria. Buses either AC or "ordinary" non-AC.
price: ₱14 from Lucena terminal, ₱43.75-117.25 from Batangas

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text:
DLTBCo., JAC, JAM and LLi, has frequent provincial service between Manila and Lucena, with most stopping in town. All buses by those companies have air-conditioning, but they can get crowded during commute hours, especially when leaving Manila.

Non-AC buses from other companies with trips to and from eastern Quezon or Bondoc Peninsula like AB Liner and P&O Transport also stop at Sariaya.

Buses stop at a designated location along General Luna near the public market, between Petron and Jollibee.

chunks.name: Get in / By car
chunks.text:
Sariaya is along the Maharlika Highway (Manila South Road, numbered Route 1/AH26) which also serves as the town's main street. The highway narrows down into General Luna Street, a two to four-lane street, and is a major bottleneck on the route in Quezon.

Sariaya will be served by one exit on the South Luzon Expressway extension to Lucena.

The beach resorts along the coast are accessible via the newer Quezon Eco-Tourism Road (Route 422).

chunks.name: Get in / By jeepney
chunks.text: Jeepneys connect Sariaya with Tiaong, Dolores, and Candelaria, as well as Tayabas and Lucena cities, and their terminals are at the same location as the bus stops. Beware though, as most services use cramped and unlicensed vehicles; taking the bus instead is cheaper, faster and more comfortable.

chunks.name: Get in / By train
chunks.text: Sariaya is also along the Philippine National Railways line running between San Pablo in Laguna and Lucena, the capital of Quezon.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text:
The town proper is fairly small, and easily explored by foot.

Tricycles connect Sariaya town proper with all other barangays, and there are terminals near the public market, and at Quezon Avenue and Magdami Street.

Along Maharlika Highway, you can take a jeepney.

chunks.name: Gala-Rodriguez Ancestral House
chunks.text:
It is an Art Deco mansion built by the renowned Filipino architect Juan Nakpil for the opulent Gala and Rodriguez families in 1935. It is one of the three houses in Sariaya declared a Heritage Home in 2008.
address: Rizal Street, Poblacion

chunks.name: Natalio Enriquez Mansion
chunks.text:
A 19th-century Beaux-Arts mansion built by a former governor of Quezon, Natalio Enriquez. It is declared a Heritage House by the Philippine government in 2008.
address: General Luna Street

chunks.name: Saint Francis of Assisi Parish Church
chunks.text:
A Barn-style Baroque church that forms the center of Sariaya's historic downtown. It was first built in 1599; the present stone church building was built in 1748, to replace one destroyed by earthquakes and flooding.
address: General Luna Street, Poblacion

chunks.name: Villa Sariaya
chunks.text:
The ancestral home of Don Catalino Rodriguez, built in Bahay na Bato (stone house) style. It was built in 1922.
address: Daliz Street, Poblacion

chunks.name: Mount Banahaw
chunks.text: An inactive volcano straddling the provinces of Laguna and Quezon. At 2170 m, it is the highest mountain in the Calabarzon region, and a sacred monument for the Tagalog people. At the side of the mountain covered by Sariaya is the breached crater wall whose collapse in 1734 triggered the emptying of Banahaw's crater lake and a massive flood that destroyed Sariaya and forced its relocation to its present site.

chunks.name: See
chunks.text: The town proper has over 150 buildings that are declared heritage sites by the Philippine government (see Wikipedia for a list). Among the most notable are:

chunks.name: Agawan Festival
chunks.text: Annual harvest festival held every May 15. Among the highlights is the Pinagong-eating contest, involving the rapid consumption of Quezon's own notoriously hard bread.

chunks.name: Sariaya Public Market
chunks.text: address: Maharlika Highway, Poblacion

chunks.name: V&V Pizza
chunks.text:
Pizza (house special, ham and cheese, Hawaiian, and pepperoni), sisig and shawarma. The location is small, and orders are done in a kiosk.
price: ₱98-192; address: 12 Magdami Street, Poblacion

chunks.name: Buddy's Restaurant
chunks.text:
A branch of a provincial restaurant chain based in Lucban serving Quezon dishes such as pancit habhab, longganisa and hardinera and has an interior decoration inspired by the Pahiyas festival.
address: Maharlika Highway corner Pablo Street, Poblacion

chunks.name: Sariaya Bread House
chunks.text:
A bakery operating since 1982 that sells local delicacies such as pinagong, a hard but sweet bread, and broas, a meringue-like contraption sold in large metal cans.
hours: 4AM-5PM; address: Maharlika Highway corner Rizal Street, Poblacion

chunks.name: Balai Sadyaya Resort
chunks.text:
Has a restaurant open 9AM-10PM.
address: Kamagong Road, Balubal

chunks.name: Villa del Prado Resort
chunks.text: address: Bignay II

chunks.name: Monte Vista Beach Resort
chunks.text: address: Bignay II

chunks.name: Sleep
chunks.text: The coastal barangays of Sariaya, to the south of the town proper, has a string of resorts along the coast of Tayabas Bay. The beaches are made of black sand of volcanic origin, so don't be fooled by the images of the resorts presenting a white-sand beachfront. Their locations are quite secluded, but you can find any of them by following the signs placed along the Eco-Tourism Road.

chunks.name: Sasmuan
chunks.text: Sasmuan is a town in southwestern Pampanga, Philippines. It is a quiet fishing town with extensive wetlands bypassed by the province's major highways.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: Sasmuan is known to have existed in the precolonial era, with its name having been derived from a Kapampangan term for a meeting place of the ancient rulers known as datus. During the Spanish occupation, its named was written as Sexmoan, with the spelling blamed on the colonizers’ inability to pronounce the native name. During the American period, the town was a subject of ridicule by English speakers, particularly US soldiers stationed in Clark, for the sexual connotations inadvertently created when the town was renamed, until in 1994, the prudish locals decided to change the name back to its indigenous spelling.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: Bypassed by major highways and notwithstanding damage caused by the Mount Pinatubo eruption in 1991, Sasmuan is a quiet fishing community sustained by the extensive wetlands of the Pampanga and Pasig-Potrero River deltas. But since the 21st century, a combination of factors such as climate change, rising sea levels, typhoons, high tide, improper land conversion and excessive groundwater extraction have irreversibly submerged numerous barangays and triggered ground subsidence across town, resulting in an increase of abandoned homes and edifices surrounded by brackish estuarine water. Looking at maps of Sasmuan, one could be forgiven to think that the town eerily resembles Venice, with thinly-stretched settlements gathered around spider web-like roads that double as dikes and fishpond fences stretching southwards into Manila Bay, where many barangays are in danger of disappearing altogether.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
Sasmuan is bypassed by the major highways of Pampanga. From Manila, take the San Fernando exit along the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) leading to the Gapan-Olongapo Road, also known as Jose Abad Santos Avenue (JASA). From San Fernando, go west towards Guagua or Lubao, where both towns have roads connecting to Sasmuan, with the one from Lubao doubling as a dike.

From Lubao and Guagua, there are tricycles servicing downtown Sasmuan. Fares from Guagua cost between P70-80, while Lubao is cheaper due to its shorter distance.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text:
Downtown Sasmuan is compact and easily accessible on foot. Tricycles are the main form of transportation between barangays.

While downtown Sasmuan is accessible by motor vehicle, a trip to the barangays and wetlands further south requires a boat.

chunks.name: Santa Lucia Parish Church
chunks.text:
Sasmuan's main Roman Catholic church, built in a Baroque style during the Spanish era and extensively modified over the succeeding years while retaining its façade and pineapple-looking cupola.
address: Santa Lucia

chunks.name: Sasmuan Coastal Wetland
chunks.text: A protected area of the Pampanga River delta on the southern edge of Sasmuan facing Manila Bay. It is a critical habitat for various flora and fauna, particularly birds, spanning 3500 ha across four barangays of Sasmuan and was internationally recognized as a Ramsar Site in 2021.

chunks.name: Sasmuan Public Market
chunks.text: address: Santa Lucia

chunks.name: Puregold Sasmuan
chunks.text: address: Guagua-Sasmuan Road, Santo Tomas

chunks.name: Sasmuan Delicacies
chunks.text: A store selling popular delicacies and sweets from town such as polvoron and turrones de casoy, a nougat made from cashew nut. Although they do not have a physical store in Sasmuan itself, they have branches in major cities in Pampanga such as San Fernando and Angeles.

chunks.name: Eat
chunks.text: A local delicacy is polvoron, a crumbly shortbread made flour, sugar, milk, nuts, and sometimes rice crispies.

chunks.name: Sleep
chunks.text: The nearest accommodations are in Guagua and Lubao.

chunks.name: Siargao
chunks.text: Siargao is an island off the coast of Mindanao in the Philippines known globally as the country's surfing capital. It is composed of eight municipalities of Surigao del Norte province, but it is treated here as one destination.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
Siargao is a beautiful paradise island with nice beaches and clear blue waters. It has now become quite a popular tourist spot with multiple flights from Manila and Cebu coming in every day. The island is well known for its surf spots (beginner and advanced), especially the Cloud 9 break where there's a big international surf contest every year.

Siargao is known for its relaxed atmosphere, friendly people and many surfer shops. Prices have increased during the last few years as more and more visitors take the trip to the island.

chunks.name: Sayak Airport
chunks.text: The island's main and only airport in the town of Del Carmen. Its only runway was able to accommodate 19-seater jets, but has since been expanded to allow flights using larger planes.

chunks.name: Get in / By plane
chunks.text:
The airport is approximately 45 minutes from the main accommodation areas at Cloud 9. Usually there are plenty of vans to transport people to their accommodation. The price is not fixed, whatever you can bargain the driver down to: they have to return to the Cloud 9 area anyway.

Cebgo has non-stop flights from Cebu four times a week, and from Manila. Prices for flights seem to vary, but expect to pay approximately ₱1500 one-way from Cebu (₱4600 from Manila). Flight time is approximately an hour from Cebu, and 2½ hours from Manila.

PAL Express has flights from Cebu and Davao. The price is approximately ₱2000 from Cebu and ₱2900 from Davao. A flight takes about an hour from either point.

chunks.name: Get in / By ferry
chunks.text:
The ferries from Surigao City to Dapa (main port town on Siargao Island) leave at approx. 6AM, 11:30AM and noon. Travel time varies from 2 hours to almost 4 hours, depending on the ferry. Fares for the ferries are ₱220/₱270 (non-air con/air con) per way.
Tricycles, vans and habal-habals (motorbikes used as taxis) wait at the pier to transport people to the main tourist/accommodation areas at Cloud 9.
Montenegro shipping lines. +63 86-2316245. has a RoRo ferry from Surigao city to Dapa. The trip takes four hours and the fare is from ₱220.
As always, flight times and ferry schedules may change without notice. The above details are current July 2016.

There is now (2025) a boat operated by 2GO running Manila-Siargao once a week each way:
Manila to Siargao: Departure: Monday, 6:30 p.m. Arrival: Tuesday, 11:30 p.m.
Siargao to Manila: Departure: Wednesday, 2:30 a.m. Arrival: Friday, 7:30 a.m.
This is a relatively luxurious boat, more like a cruise ship than a mundane ferry.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text:
For the non-surf people, you can explore the island by motorbike or boat. You can go island jumping, scuba diving and snorkeling.
And there's also many caves and waterfalls to explore.

chunks.name: Fat Lips Surfshop
chunks.text:
Offers new/used/rental surfboards, apparel, and surf accessories. They also arrange island hopping and other tours.
hours: Daily 8AM-9PM; address: Purok 5, Bayud, General Luna

chunks.name: Tagpuan Cafe
chunks.text:
Here you can have some shrimps or crabs.
hours: Daily 10AM-9PM; address: Sunrise Blvd, Kiosk #7

chunks.name: Drink
chunks.text:
If you want to hang out at night, catch a beer and some food, enjoy good music and meet new people, you're in luck: no shortage here.

BARREL: Beachfront Sports Bar, in General Luna next to Siago Beach Resort. A beachside bar. +63 938 233 2292

chunks.name: Sleep
chunks.text:
Look for accommodation around General Luna ("GL") or Cloud 9, where there's a number of places by the beach. GL is the main village near some of the main surf spots, a 5-minute drive (₱30 per person) from Cloud 9. Cloud 9 has places to eat (more limited) and is walking distance from the pro and beginner surf spot. Food here is more expensive, but accommodation is still cheap.

In Siargao, accommodations in the "budget" category cost under ₱700 per room per night.

chunks.name: Happy Gecko Siargao Backpackers Hostel.
chunks.text: price: Dorm bed ₱250 per person; address: Cloud 9 Boardwalk

chunks.name: Wayfarers Cloud 9 Restaurant & Residences
chunks.text:
Fan double rooms with own bathrooms.
price: From ₱650; address: Cloud 9

chunks.name: Sleep / Budget
chunks.text:
Paglaom Hostel. +63 9999900308. Dorm bed ₱250.
Hangout Siargao. +63 9276116117. dorm bed ₱250.
Ocean 101 Beach Resort. North of Cloud Nine. +63 9108480893. Fan room from +63 500.
Vila Solaria. South of Cloud Nine. +63 9204077730. Dorm bed 300.
Siargao Surfer's Lodge. +63 9283747447. Dorm bed ₱250.

chunks.name: Siargao Surf Resort
chunks.text:
Set in the heart of the Siargao Island Surf community.
price: From ₱2500; address: Catangnan

chunks.name: Malipaya Siargao
chunks.text:
Malipaya Villas offers beachfront glamping tent accommodations along Tourism Road. Each spacious 30-square-meter tent includes two queen-sized beds, air conditioning, and a private bathroom. The tent area features an outdoor lanai that can serve as a lounge or dining space. Guests have access to a private swimming pool and direct beach access.
address: Bongayon, Purok Uno

chunks.name: Go next
chunks.text:
Cebu by air.
Surigao city by ferry.
Transportation off the island is via Cebu Pacific flights to/from Cebu or by ferry 7 days per week to/from Surigao City. You can fly to Manila, Palawan or Boracay via Cebu.

chunks.name: Siaton
chunks.text: Siaton is a municipality at the southern tip of Negros Island, in Negros Oriental Province, Philippines. Population was about 83,000 in the 2020 census.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
Most people reach Siaton via the coastal highway that runs through the town, often either by bus or jeepney. It is about 55 km from Dumaguete or 250 km from Bacolod. The highway in both directions is good; some roads leading off it, e.g. to Tambobo Bay, are not.

Other people arrive by boat; this is a major harbour for yachts.

There has been some discussion of building a small airport for Siaton, but as of mid-2023 no plan has been announced.

chunks.name: Lake Balanan
chunks.text: This is a scenic mountain lake in a protected wildlife area, in Siaton Municipality a few km inland from the town.

chunks.name: Tillys Sail Tour
chunks.text: A sailing family residing in Tambobo Bay, offers sailing tours as well as boat repair for world cruisers.

chunks.name: Buy
chunks.text:
There are usually some yachts for sale at Tambobo Bay.

Some of these vessels are more-or-less abandoned; their owners have settled in some Philippine city, or flown back to Australia, or whatever. Some can be had at quite attractive prices if you bargain well, though not all owners will accept a low price. Caution is advised since a boat that has not had regular maintenance for some time may develop all sorts of expensive problems. In the worst case, a boat might not be worth taking on even if the owner were giving it away.

The Western owner, Nigel, at Tonga Sail is a boat builder.

chunks.name: Tonga Sail Inn Retreat
chunks.text:
Extremely basic accommodation. Good Western restaurant.
price: ₱300

chunks.name: Cove Sands Beach Resort
chunks.text:
A beach resort located on its own secluded bay. Personalized service. Fan cottages and air-con rooms. Private bathrooms, hot water showers, Free Wi-Fi and morning coffee and bottled water in all rooms.
price: ₱1000; address: Bonbonon

chunks.name: Antulang Beach Resort
chunks.text:
High-end place with swimming pool and library, a/c in all rooms, breakfast included.
price: ₱1700 and up

chunks.name: Sibonga
chunks.text: Sibonga is a municipality in Cebu Province. Population was about 48,000 in the 2015 census.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
Sibonga is best known for the Marist Monastery of the Holy Eucharist and a church called Simala Miraculous Mama Mary. They are in a single large building complex, and exceedingly scenic. For Catholics, especially Filipinos, this is a place of pilgrimage.

As in many Philippine municipalities, most of the population is along the coast. The monastery and church complex, however, is some distance inland.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text:
Sibonga is on the coastal highway that rings Cebu Island. It is the next municipality south of Carcar, which is the southernmost town of the Metro Cebu urban area.

The usual way to reach Sibonga by bus is on a Ceres bus from the South Bus Station in Cebu City. Buses bound for Dumaguete or Oslob pass through Sibonga.

chunks.name: Do
chunks.text:
The feast day of Saint Philomena, the town's patron saint, on June 10th is the town's main fiesta. Some locals also celebrate the Sinulog festival in late January.

The Pastores de Sibonga is a Christmas show put on every year in Magcagong Barangay. It recounts the nativity in song and dance, using at least four dancers.

chunks.name: Go next
chunks.text:
Metro Cebu, not far to the north, is the region's main urban center.
Going south, one might visit Oslob which is known for whale watching, or cross a narrow strait to the next island (Negros) and the tourist town Dumaguete.
Across the island to the west is the diving destination Moalboal.

chunks.name: Sigay
chunks.text: Sigay is a municipality in Ilocos Sur. Situated within the Cordillera mountains, it is home to the tallest waterfall in the Ilocos Region.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
Sigay is a landlocked municipality established along a tributary of the Amburayan River. It is a highland town in the Cordillera mountains and has significant Igorot communities. Formerly a part of the Amburayan subdistrict of Mountain Province, it was annexed by Ilocos Sur in 1920. The area saw heavy fighting in World War II during the Battle of Bessang Pass in 1945, when Allied forces struggled to break through Japanese defenses in Bessang Ridge on their way to liberate Baguio and the Luzon Cordilleras.

Sigay is the least populated municipality of Ilocos Sur, with a population of only 2,577 people as of 2024. The main economic activities are coffee and rice terrace farming, and nature-based tourism, through poor road infrastructure tends to keep most visitors at bay.

chunks.name: Get in
chunks.text: Sigay is one of the more isolated towns of Ilocos Sur, being completely bypassed by its major highways. Instead, it is connected to a secondary road leading south towards Urzadan Bridge in the neighboring municipality of Suyo, which is along Tagudin-Cervantes-Sabangan Road running between Mountain Province and Manila North Road in the coastal town of Tagudin. To the northwest, another secondary road leads to the neighboring municipality of Salcedo and onwards to Candon, the most populated city in Ilocos Sur. Both roads feature scenic mountain drives and frightening hairpin curves.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text: Tricycles are the main form of transportation in town, but due to the uneven terrain, a 4WD is recommended. Most tourist attractions are only accessible through extended hikes.

chunks.name: Aw-asen Falls
chunks.text:
The main tourist draw in Sigay, it is the tallest waterfall in Ilocos Region, with a height of 110 m gushing through a vertical rock face. Access to the site is restricted to pre-organized tour groups for safety reasons.
address: Santo Rosario

chunks.name: Mount Tuwato
chunks.text:
A 1802 m peak along the Bessang Ridge shared with the municipality of Cervantes.
address: San Elias

chunks.name: Mount Monserrat
chunks.text:
A 1763 m high peak along the Bessang Ridge.
address: San Elias

chunks.name: Mount Longon
chunks.text:
Another mountain in the Bessang Ridge, often climbed as part of the Tuwato-Monserrat circuit.
address: San Elias

chunks.name: Namempengan Falls
chunks.text:
An overlooked but similarly picturesque terraced waterfall system gushing along a shredded-looking and gently sloped rock face on the other side of town.
address: Mabileg

chunks.name: Sigay Viewdeck
chunks.text:
A panoramic viewdeck on the boundary with Suyo with vistas over Sigay's valleys.
address: Santo Rosario

chunks.name: Buy
chunks.text: There is no market to speak of, only a few mom-and-pop sari-sari stores. There are also no banks or ATMs, so bring plenty of cash.

chunks.name: Silang
chunks.text: Silang is a rural municipality in Cavite, along Aguinaldo Highway. It shares a mildly cool climate with its southern neighbor, Tagaytay, but is somewhat off the beaten track.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text:
Silang is bordered by Dasmariñas, General Mariano Alvarez, and Carmona to the north, General Trias and Amadeo on the west, Tagaytay to the south and by Laguna province to the east. It is a landlocked municipality with 64 barangays.

Silang is rather overshadowed by nearby Tagaytay, but has a similar cool climate, and a few sights that can be visited within a day. The municipality has a large Korean community, who reside here as living is cheaper than in Tagaytay. The Seventh-Day Adventist Church in the Philippines is headquartered in this area, and they host an Adventist university along the highway between Santa Rosa and Tagaytay. The Philippine National Police also has its main academy nearby. Silang has many subdivisions housing some of the Filipino elites and some expats. Economic growth is making inroads through the real estate boom, so living costs slowly increase despite being rural.

chunks.name: Erjohn and Almark
chunks.text: Bus station near Monteluce, on barangay Lalaan 1.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text:
Silang is easily reached by bus through Aguinaldo Highway. It takes over 1 hour or even 2 from Manila due to traffic jams to the north, but can be short as 10-15 minutes from Tagaytay.

Other than from Erjohn and Almark, most buses passing through Silang don't have their own dedicated bus stations, but all the other companies serving Silang can drop you off anywhere along Aguinaldo Highway if you request. Most important for travellers are the stops along a stretch of Aguinaldo Highway that bypasses the town to the west (as Bypass Road).

chunks.name: Get in / By car
chunks.text:
Two major highways pass through Silang. Aguinaldo Highway (Route 419 to the north, unnumbered at the bypass west of Poblacion, and Route 410 to the south), a four-lane at-grade highway, serves the town proper and the western portion of Silang. Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road (Route 420), which is being widened to four lanes, lies to the eastern side of the municipality.

From the northeast, there is the two-lane Carmona-Silang Road (Kaong Road), connecting the town proper with Governor's Drive (Route 65) in Carmona, but it is a narrow road through villages and jungle.

Silang is along the four-lane tolled Cavite-Laguna Expressway (CALAx). The relevant exits for Silang are at Silang East in Kaong, involving travel through narrow rural roads; and Silang West exit, connecting with Aguinaldo Highway.

chunks.name: Get in / By jeepney
chunks.text:
Jeepneys ply both highways, and is the only public transport option along Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road.

Along Aguinaldo Highway, jeepneys run from Tagaytay down to Dasmariñas and Imus. Most enter the town proper, but some use the bypass instead.

On Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Rd, there is only one route, the Balibago-Tagaytay route. As of 2025, most jeepneys on this route are franchised vehicles, but unlicensed colorum jeeps still ply the route and must be avoided. It is the only option to the eastern side of the municipality, and you'll likely have to take this if you travel via Santa Rosa by bus.

chunks.name: Get in / By van
chunks.text: Passenger vans operate from Calamba, Laguna along the Balibago-Tagaytay route.

chunks.name: Get around
chunks.text:
Tricycles are the primary mode of transportation through town and its barangays. Jeepneys are the most economical way to travel along the areas beside Aguinaldo Highway.

Most of Silang is in the countryside, dotted with barangays and crisscrossed by a network of local roads. Travelling by car is advisable if you want to avoid the hassle with tricycles, but watch out as roads are narrow and there are lots of pedestrian traffic through the barangays.

chunks.name: Lucsuhin Natural Bridge
chunks.text:
It is a natural bridge formation between Barangay Lucsuhin and Kalubkob in Silang, Cavite. The formation crosses the Ylang-Ylang River and is the first, large natural bridge reported in the country. The bridge and cave is not a protected area.
address: Lucsuhin and Kalubkob

chunks.name: Silang Church
chunks.text:
A typical Baroque church dedicated to the Virgin of Candelaria. The original parish church and its attached school was completed 1595 by the Franciscans, but were destroyed by fire in 1603. A new church was built in 1637-39, and dedicated in 1640, and its belfry was damaged by earthquakes in 1880 and repaired in 1989. It became a Spanish Civil Guard (Guardia Civil) outpost against a local uprising by Filipino general Vito Belarmino during the Philippine Revolution in 1896.
address: J. P. Rizal Street, Poblacion

chunks.name: Perlas ng Silang
chunks.text:
Meaning "Pearl of Silang", it is a 3.5 ha flower farm featuring an assorted number of flowering plants, manicured gardens and lawns, and sculpted horticultural images.
price: ₱120; address: Purok 5, Pulong Bunga

chunks.name: Riviera Golf Course and Country Club
chunks.text:
36 holes, has a Korean restaurant. The course's terrain is flat, but challenging due to winds, but the weather is generally clear and temperatures are cooler.
hours: Mon-Sat 5AM-7PM, Sun 5AM-7:30PM; address: Bypass Road, Aguinaldo Highway, Biluso

chunks.name: Acienda Designer Outlet
chunks.text:
Opened 2018, this open-air outlet mall houses a collection of 100 designer clothing shops in four European-themed sections. Its main catch is that most items are 70% off the tag price, all year round. There is also a small foodcourt and a branch of Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf, a domestic coffeeshop chain.
address: KM 48 Aguinaldo Highway, Lalaan Primero

chunks.name: Ilog Maria Honeybee Farm
chunks.text:
Large assortment of products sourced from the farm's honeybees such as soap, propolis and royal jelly, shampoo, and Honey Cider vinegar. Their throat spray is quite effective for smokers.
hours: 8AM–5PM; address: 4118 Aguinaldo Highway, Lalaan I

chunks.name: Santis Delicatessen
chunks.text:
A branch of a Metro Manila-based delicatessen store. They also sell ready-to-ear deli sandwiches and sweets.
hours: 8AM-8:30PM Sun-Thu, 8AM-9:30PM Fri-Sat; address: Aguinaldo Highway, Buho

chunks.name: Silang Public Market
chunks.text: address: M. Belen Street, San Miguel II

chunks.name: Vista Mall Silang
chunks.text: address: Aguinaldo Highway, Biga

chunks.name: WalterMart Silang
chunks.text: hours: 9AM–9PM; address: Aguinaldo Highway corner Biluso Road, San Vicente II

chunks.name: Premier Plaza
chunks.text: address: Aguinaldo Highway, Lucsuhin

chunks.name: Puregold Silang
chunks.text: address: Aguinaldo Highway

chunks.name: Primark Center Silang
chunks.text: hours: 8AM-8PM; address: Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road, Tartaria

chunks.name: Robinsons Easymart Maguyam
chunks.text: hours: 7AM-10PM; address: Maguyam Road, Maguyam

chunks.name: Balinsasayaw
chunks.text:
They serve good Filipino food inside bahay kubo cottages, with fly and mosquito netting, fans, and power outlets. The restaurant has a second branch at the junction with Aguinaldo Highway and J. Rizal Street in Barangay Lucsuhin leading to Silang town proper, beside Premier Plaza.
hours: 9AM-9PM; address: KM 48 Aguinaldo Highway, Lalaan 1

chunks.name: Aling Tonya's Seafood Palutuan
chunks.text:
A seafood restaurant that has operated since 1974 and serves fresh seafood despite its inland location by keeping live specimen to be cooked upon order.

chunks.name: Silay
chunks.text: Silay City is dubbed as the Paris of Negros because of its European-inspired houses which have been declared historical landmarks, and it is the second museum city in the Philippines next to Vigan. Silay is a center for arts, culture and ecotourism and might be as close as the province can get to the dazzling streets of Europe because of its well-preserved European colonial houses.

chunks.name: Understand / History
chunks.text:
A local legend tells of how Silay City got its name. There once lived a princess named Kansilay. An attack on the settlement by pirates was thwarted when the princess bravely led the people in the village's defense. The fight was furious and the princess fought like a seasoned warrior. Murals that used to grace some of the city's public buildings depict her as a fierce fighter wielding a huge talibong, a short native single-edged sword. The pirates were routed, but at the cost of the princess' life. Her paramour arrived in time to see her die. In grief, the people lovingly buried her. To their surprise, a tree grew right over her grave, the first Kansilay tree, a final gift from the brave princess.

The city has many annual and monthly events that were established many years ago which Silaynons and the people from different cities enjoys such as their festival called as Kansilay Festival. Silay's also known for their heritage houses, old antique landmarks and other historical places. The transportation system is good, and a variety of tasty restaurants and good architecture are available for visitors to enjoy.

chunks.name: Understand / Climate
chunks.text: Silay City has two kind of seasons, the wet season, and the dry season. Silaynon's adapted to this kind of climate. For wet season, they usually bring umbrellas, raincoats, or any water-resistant accessories just to prevent the rain. While for the dry season, they usually put SPF lotions and moisturizers over their body and also bring umbrellas to prevent the sun rays and heat from the sun. It is also one of Filipino's fun traditional activity; kids love to play in the rain and splash and squish on the wate. It's also fun to sunbathe on a beach with the sun. The dry season usually starts in February and ends in April while the wet season usually starts May onward.

chunks.name: Understand / Language
chunks.text: Silaynons official dialect is Hiligaynon or Ilonggo while some can talk Tagalog (national language), Cebuano, and Ilokano. Some of the Silaynons can speak fluently in English. Communicating at them aren't difficult so no worries. Filipino people can understand English for it's the second known language in the Philippines.

chunks.name: Bacolod-Silay Airport
chunks.text: Served by the two airlines and connects Silay and the whole of Negros Occidental with Manila, Cebu and Davao. Cebu Pacific: Manila, Cebu, Davao. Philippine Airlines: Manila, Cebu.

chunks.name: Get in / By plane
chunks.text: Take a taxi or minivan from Silay airport to Silay city proper on arrival. There are also vans to the provincial capital, Bacolod.

chunks.name: Get in / By bus
chunks.text:
Silay is about 30-45 minutes away from Bacolod. The Ceres bus is 3 times faster than an ordinary bus. There are also buses to/from many destinations including Sipalay, Talisay, Victorias and Kabankalan.

Fares from Bacolod to/from Silay, the bus depends by kilometers. The fare will change without any notice. Students/senior citizen/people with disabilities: ₱13-15 (regular buses); ₱13-20 (aircon buses); ₱20-100 (special buses). Regular fares: ₱15-20 (regular buses); ₱20-30 (aircon buses); ₱30-200 (special buses).

chunks.name: Get in / By taxi
chunks.text: Taxis are the best option for getting around Silay. However, some of them might offer you a fixed price because of distance or because you're a tourist. If they do offer you a fixed price don't accept it, get out of the taxi as soon as possible and look for another one or try threatening the driver that you will call the police as fixed prices are illegal. Always pay according to the meter and keep a close watch at the meter as some of the drivers might cheat you. If you plan to give a tip, round off the fare. For example if it is ₱90, give him ₱100 and also tell him to keep the change. Flag down rate for taxis is ₱40.

chunks.name: Get in / By tricycle
chunks.text:
Tricycles are small and often cramped for two people; however, they're the cheapest mode of transportation for getting around alone.

From the age of 12-19, the starting point is ₱6-10. From the age of 20 and above, the starting point is ₱8-15. Adults such as parents or working individuals, the starting point is ₱8-20. These fares are from/to all destinations within Silay City only. For further destinations, try buses, jeepneys or taxis. Tricycle fares can change without any notice.

chunks.name: Get in / By jeepneys
chunks.text:
The cheapest mode of transportation if you choose not to travel alone, it is the local version of buses. Don't forget to ask for a discount if you're a senior citizen or a student. Flag down rates for jeepneys nationwide is ₱7, jeepneys have fixed routes. One can easily go anywhere in Silay by riding a tricycle which cost ₱8 per passenger within the city limits only. Riding a jeepney to Bacolod will cost ₱15 per passenger and ₱18 on air conditioned shuttles.

If you have problems to any transportation vehicles when it comes to fares and services, you can call the LTFRB hotline number: +63 34 (426-2515).

After the death of their father; Victor Gaston, the family abandoned the house and fell into ruins but during the 1970s concerned people showed their support and repaired the house. The architecture is a typical example of "Bahay na bato" or House of stone, with American-European colonial influences. Today it is a museum containing antiques.

chunks.name: San Diego Pro-Cathedral
chunks.text: The only pro-Cathedral church outside Metro Manila, its birth was in the 1700s, the church was still made of nipa-palm, bamboo and grass, in the 1800s the church was then made into a wood and stone structure, finally in the 1900s the structure was made into what it is now, the architecture; Lucio Bernasconi (an Italian architect) took churches in his native Italy as an influence and model of the church. It was finished on 1927 also inaugurated in the same year.

chunks.text: Simunul is a coastal municipality in the island province of Tawi-Tawi in Bangsamoro. It is home to some relics of what is believed to be the first mosque in the Philippines, the Sheik Karimul Makhdum Mosque, mostly built in the 1960s.

chunks.name: Understand
chunks.text: Its population in 2020 was 34,245. The language spoken is Sama, also known as Sinama. The first Muslims in the Philippines are said to have arrived at Simunur.
